Restrictive disease: cautious diuresis, treat cause; Takotsubo: supportive care after excluding ACS
Myocarditis with shock → ICU, circulatory support; no routine antiviral or immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Sudden cardiac death, atrial fibrillation, thromboembolism; advanced failure → transplantation evaluation
★ HCM with cardiac arrest or major sudden-death risk → **ICD** consideration

rows.label: Prevention
items: Screen first-degree relatives in inherited disease; avoid cardiotoxins
Myocarditis: restrict strenuous exercise until clinical recovery and reassessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic cardiomyopathy: obstructive coronary disease explains dysfunction
Constrictive pericarditis: pericardial disease, respiratory ventricular interdependence
Aortic stenosis: murmur softer with standing/Valsalva, unlike obstructive HCM

table.title: Echo phenotype
rows: Enlarged ventricles, diffuse hypokinesia, reduced EF
Transient apical ballooning beyond coronary territory

cardiomyopathies.evidence: HCM checked 2026-10-30: [AHA/ACC 2024](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/05/06/15/12/2024-hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy-gl); other content established teaching.

caustic-ingestion.name: Caustic ingestion
caustic-ingestion.scope: Acid and alkali ingestion, airway assessment, contraindications to emesis or neutralization, early esophagogastroduodenoscopy within 24 hours, stricture complications
caustic-ingestion.core: Corrosive ingestion can burn the airway and gastrointestinal tract; a normal mouth examination does not exclude deep injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young children: accidental household cleaner exposure; adults: intentional large-volume ingestion
Drain/oven cleaners (NaOH), industrial acids; bleach usually mild; concentration, contact time determine severity

rows.label: Clues
items: Oral burns/ulcers, drooling, odynophagia, dysphagia, vomiting, hematemesis, chest or abdominal pain
★ **Stridor, hoarseness, respiratory distress** → threatened airway
Severe tenderness, rigidity, fever, shock → transmural necrosis or perforation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alkali: liquefactive necrosis, deep esophageal penetration; acid: coagulative necrosis, often gastric injury
Both agents can injure the entire upper gastrointestinal tract; eschar provides incomplete protection

rows.label: Dx
items: Identify substance, concentration, amount, time; poison control consultation
★ Stable symptomatic/significant exposure → **EGD within 24 hours** for injury grading
Suspected perforation/necrosis → contrast CT chest/abdomen and surgery consultation; avoid diagnostic endoscopy if perforated
CBC, electrolytes, renal function, lactate, blood gas; normal labs cannot exclude injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Airway first**; early controlled intubation with direct visualization when swelling progresses
NPO, IV crystalloid, analgesia; surgical treatment for perforation or full-thickness necrosis
★ **No emesis, neutralization, gastric lavage, or activated charcoal**; additional burns or heat generation
Avoid blind NG placement; no routine corticosteroids or prophylactic antibiotics

rows.label: Complications
items: Mediastinitis, peritonitis, hemorrhage, fistula; delayed esophageal stricture or gastric outlet obstruction
Long-term esophageal squamous cell carcinoma risk; strictures may require repeated dilation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Locked storage in original labeled containers; never transfer chemicals into beverage bottles
Intentional ingestion → psychiatric assessment after stabilization; swallowing/nutrition follow-up after severe injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Esophageal foreign body: discrete obstruction on history or imaging
Pill esophagitis: medication exposure, focal ulceration without extensive chemical burns

caustic-ingestion.evidence: Not checked online; established toxicology teaching.

celiac-disease.name: Celiac disease
celiac-disease.scope: Gluten-sensitive enteropathy, malabsorption, iron deficiency anemia, dermatitis herpetiformis, IgA anti-tTG, small bowel villous atrophy, gluten-free diet
celiac-disease.core: Gluten-triggered autoimmune small-bowel injury causing malabsorption or unexplained iron deficiency, sometimes with intensely pruritic extensor-surface dermatitis herpetiformis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: First-degree relative, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune thyroid disease, selective IgA deficiency
HLA-DQ2/DQ8 susceptibility; positive genotype common and not diagnostic

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea, bloating, weight loss; constipation or minimal GI symptoms possible
Iron deficiency refractory to oral replacement, aphthous ulcers, low bone density
Children: poor growth/delayed puberty; severe disease: hypoalbuminemia, edema, vitamin deficiencies

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tissue transglutaminase modifies gliadin → T-cell response damages proximal intestinal mucosa
Impaired absorption → iron/folate deficiency; cutaneous granular IgA deposition causes rash
Fat malabsorption → **vitamin D deficiency** → low calcium + low phosphate; hypoparathyroidism instead raises phosphate

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ While **eating gluten → IgA anti-tTG (or anti-endomysial) + total IgA**; gluten restriction causes false negatives
★ IgA deficiency → **IgG anti-tTG or deamidated gliadin peptide antibodies**
★ Adults: positive serology or high suspicion → **EGD with multiple duodenal biopsies**, even if mucosa normal
Biopsy: villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, intraepithelial lymphocytes; high suspicion overrides negative serology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Lifelong gluten-free diet**: avoid wheat, barley, rye; dietitian, cross-contamination counseling
Pure uncontaminated oats usually tolerated; replace iron, folate, calcium, vitamin D and other measured deficiencies
Dermatitis herpetiformis: dapsone for rapid relief after G6PD testing; diet treats underlying intestinal injury
Persistent symptoms → assess gluten exposure, alternative diagnoses; refractory disease → specialist before immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Osteoporosis, infertility; untreated disease → enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, small-bowel adenocarcinoma
Dapsone → hemolysis/methemoglobinemia; restrictive diet → nutritional imbalance

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Follow **symptoms, nutritional labs, anti-tTG trend**; persistent elevation suggests gluten exposure
Bone-density assessment in adults with risk/malabsorption; test symptomatic first-degree relatives
No proven primary prevention; do not start gluten exclusion before diagnostic testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no objective malabsorption, anemia, or inflammatory injury
Giardiasis: contaminated water exposure, stool antigen/PCR positive
Pancreatic insufficiency: low fecal elastase, **normal D-xylose absorption** (low in mucosal disease)

cerebral-palsy.name: Cerebral palsy
cerebral-palsy.scope: Spastic diplegia, spastic hemiplegia, spastic quadriplegia, dyskinetic (athetoid) cerebral palsy, ataxic, prematurity and intraventricular hemorrhage risk, hyperreflexia, contractures, multidisciplinary management
cerebral-palsy.core: Persistent abnormal posture and movement from a nonprogressive injury to the developing brain; functional manifestations change with growth.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prematurity, periventricular leukomalacia, intraventricular hemorrhage, perinatal stroke
Congenital infection, brain malformation, neonatal hypoxic-ischemic injury, kernicterus

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Delayed motor milestones**, persistent primitive reflexes, abnormal tone; early hand preference suggests hemiplegia
Spasticity: velocity-dependent tone, hyperreflexia, clonus, extensor plantar responses
Feeding difficulty, drooling, asymmetric posture; cognition may be normal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immature motor pathways injured before, during, or shortly after birth; injury itself remains static

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical developmental/neurologic assessment**; brain MRI defines injury pattern or malformation
Assess hearing, vision, communication, nutrition, epilepsy, and intellectual function
Loss of acquired skills or progressive weakness → metabolic/genetic evaluation rather than presumed cerebral palsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Early multidisciplinary rehabilitation**: physical, occupational, speech and feeding support
Focal spasticity → botulinum toxin; generalized troublesome spasticity → oral baclofen
Severe refractory spasticity → intrathecal baclofen or selected dorsal rhizotomy
Orthoses, mobility aids; fixed contractures/hip displacement → orthopedic evaluation
Treat seizures; swallowing assessment and enteral feeding when aspiration or inadequate intake

rows.label: Complications
items: Contractures, hip subluxation, scoliosis, pain, osteoporosis; aspiration, malnutrition, epilepsy
Musculoskeletal deformities can progress despite static brain lesion

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Antenatal magnesium sulfate** for imminent early preterm birth reduces cerebral palsy risk
Treat severe neonatal hyperbilirubinemia; therapeutic hypothermia for eligible neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
Hip surveillance, stretching, adequate nutrition reduce secondary disability

rows.label: Mimics
items: Muscular dystrophy: progressive proximal weakness, elevated CK
Dopa-responsive dystonia: diurnal fluctuation, marked levodopa response

cerebral-palsy.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric neurology and perinatal prevention teaching.

child-growth-and-development.name: Child growth and development
child-growth-and-development.scope: Normal growth velocity, weight doubling and tripling milestones, WHO/CDC growth chart interpretation, developmental surveillance, normal toddler behavioral variants (head banging, temper tantrums)
child-growth-and-development.core: Interpret serial growth and developmental progress against age, family pattern, and corrected gestational age; a trajectory matters more than one percentile.

rows.label: Definition
items: Weight doubles by 4–6 months, triples by 12 months, quadruples near 24 months
Length increases about 25 cm during year 1; prepubertal height velocity about 5–6 cm/year
★ **WHO charts before 2 years; CDC charts from 2 years** in US practice

rows.label: Interpret
items: Nutrition failure: weight falls first; endocrine disease: height slows with preserved/increased weight
★ Falling **2 major percentile channels**, well child → **diet diary, calorie counts** before labs
Correct prematurity through about 2 years; track infant head circumference

rows.label: Use when
items: Developmental surveillance every visit; standardized general screens at 9, 18, and 30 months
★ **Regression/missed milestones → early intervention**; language delay → **audiometry** before speech testing
BMI-for-age from 2 years; weight-for-length younger; consider parental heights and pubertal timing

rows.label: Compare
items: Tantrums, picky eating, bedtime separation distress → reassure, routines, calm limits; no sedatives
Head banging at sleep onset or frustration, normal development → self-soothing; assess injuries
Preschool restlessness, good function → no stimulants; overwhelmed parent → **parenting classes**

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **One percentile cannot diagnose disease**; stable tracking + normal exam → reassure
Persistent skill loss needs evaluation; never wait for school failure
Short parents, normal bone age → familial; average parents, delayed puberty → **constitutional delay**

rows.label: Adolescence
items: ★ Moodiness, privacy, family detachment, rule-questioning, late bedtimes, good function → reassure, educate parents
Parental-pressure conflict, occasional experimentation, no impairment → not ODD, substance use disorder
Weight worry, stable percentile, normal BMI, regular menses → normal; not eating disorder

table.title: Normal by age
rows: Holds head up; not yet reaching
Sits unsupported; bangs blocks, self-feeds finger foods
Walks; scribbles; non-walker at 14 months normal
Balances on one foot; copies circle
Same-sex parent preference; involve other parent otherwise

child-growth-and-development.evidence: Checked screening ages 2026-10-30: [AAP surveillance/screening](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-surveillance-and-screening-patient-care/); growth facts established pediatric teaching.

chlamydia-infection.name: Chlamydia infection
chlamydia-infection.scope: Chlamydia trachomatis, nongonococcal urethritis, cervicitis, lymphogranuloma venereum, neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonia, NAAT screening and diagnosis, doxycycline and azithromycin
chlamydia-infection.core: Often silent sexually transmitted intracellular infection causing urethritis or cervicitis; untreated infection threatens fertility and can infect newborns during delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25 years, new/multiple partners, inconsistent condom use, infected partner; perinatal exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, scant discharge, sterile pyuria; friable cervix, mucopurulent discharge, postcoital/intermenstrual bleeding
★ Neonatal conjunctivitis at **5–12 days**; afebrile staccato pneumonia at **1–3 months**
LGV: transient painless genital ulcer → tender inguinal nodes/buboes or invasive proctocolitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: C. trachomatis: obligate intracellular bacterium; D–K serovars cause genital/perinatal infection, L1–L3 cause LGV

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT**: vaginal swab preferred in women; first-catch urine in men; rectal swab after exposure
Test for gonorrhea, HIV, syphilis; fever, pelvic pain, cervical motion tenderness → evaluate for PID
Infant conjunctival testing requires epithelial cells; nasopharyngeal testing for pneumonia
Sexually active MSM: annual site-specific screening; every 3–6 months with persistent high risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated infection → **doxycycline for 7 days**; LGV → 21 days
★ Pregnancy → **azithromycin**, single dose; alternative when adherence doubtful, less reliable for rectal infection
Neonatal disease → oral erythromycin for 14 days; azithromycin alternative; topical treatment alone inadequate
Gonorrhea suspected or detected → add ceftriaxone; PID requires broader multidrug coverage

rows.label: Complications
items: PID → tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; epididymitis, reactive arthritis
LGV → rectal strictures/fistulas; infant macrolides → hypertrophic pyloric stenosis risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; expedited partner treatment where legal
Abstain until 7-day course completed or 7 days after single dose, and partners treated
★ **Annual NAAT**: sexually active women <25 despite condoms; older if risk; pregnancy entry; Pap from 21
Retest at 3 months; pregnancy test-of-cure at 4 weeks; neonatal eye ointment does not prevent chlamydia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gonorrhea: copious purulent discharge, Gram-stain intracellular diplococci; **neutrophils alone** → nongonococcal urethritis, usually chlamydia
M. genitalium: persistent nongonococcal urethritis after doxycycline; separate NAAT
HSV: painful ulcers and external dysuria rather than isolated cervical discharge
Cystitis: suprapubic tenderness, bacteriuria; urethritis → **distal anterior vaginal wall tenderness**, sterile pyuria

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.name: Chromosomal and genetic disorders
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.scope: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner syndrome (45,X0), Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY), Fragile X syndrome (FMR1 trinucleotide repeat), Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes, DiGeorge syndrome (22q11 deletion)
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.core: Recognize syndromic combinations of growth, cognition, gonadal function, dysmorphism, and congenital malformations; confirm with the correct genetic test.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced maternal age: meiotic nondisjunction; balanced parental translocation: recurrent aneuploid pregnancy
Family expansion history: repeat disorders; microdeletions often de novo

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Down** (trisomy 21): hypotonia, upslanting fissures, epicanthal folds, macroglossia, single palmar crease, AV septal defect
DiGeorge: conotruncal defect, cleft palate, absent thymus, hypocalcemic tetany
Turner: newborn hand/foot lymphedema, redundant nuchal skin; later nevi
**Williams** (7q11.23 deletion): overfriendly, elfin facies, hyperacusis, intellectual disability, supravalvular stenosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **Genomic imprinting**: parent-specific expression; deletion or uniparental disomy can disrupt the active copy
22q11 deletion disrupts pharyngeal pouch development → T-cell deficiency and hypoparathyroidism

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected Down, Turner, Klinefelter → **karyotype**; prenatal screening alone never establishes diagnosis
Microarray: microdeletion; targeted repeat analysis: fragile X; methylation testing: imprinting disorders
Down: assess heart, hearing, vision, thyroid; DiGeorge: calcium and lymphocyte subsets

rows.label: Tx
items: Early developmental services, speech support; repair congenital defects
Turner: growth hormone then estrogen/progestin; Klinefelter: testosterone after endocrine assessment
Prader-Willi: supervised food access; Angelman: seizure management; DiGeorge: calcium and infection management

rows.label: Complications
items: Down: duodenal atresia (double bubble), leukemia, early Alzheimer disease, atlantoaxial instability
Turner: coarctation, bicuspid valve, aortic dissection; Klinefelter: infertility, breast cancer
Prader-Willi: severe obesity; DiGeorge: severe infections and later psychiatric disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Genetic counseling**: recurrence depends on nondisjunction, translocation, imprinting mechanism, or repeat expansion
Avoid live vaccines with severe T-cell deficiency; use irradiated blood for profound immunodeficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Noonan syndrome: Turner-like habitus, normal chromosomes; either sex, pulmonic stenosis
Congenital hypothyroidism: hypotonia and delayed development; abnormal newborn thyroid screen
Constitutional delay: delayed bone age; no edema or nevi
Rett: girls with regression; MECP2 variant

table.title: Distinctive genotype–phenotype pairs
rows: Short female, webbed neck, streak ovaries, primary amenorrhea
Tall male, small firm testes, gynecomastia, high FSH/LH
FMR1 CGG expansion at X fragile site; silencing
Long face, large ears, macroorchidism, autism-like behavior
IUGR, clenched overlapping fingers, prominent occiput, micrognathia, VSD

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established genetics teaching.

chronic-kidney-disease.name: Chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease
chronic-kidney-disease.scope: CKD progression, anemia of CKD (erythropoietin deficiency), mineral and bone disorder, uremic complications, volume overload, indications for emergent dialysis (AEIOU), vascular access
chronic-kidney-disease.core: Persistent kidney injury or reduced filtration causes progressive cardiovascular, metabolic and uremic complications; dialysis follows clinical indications rather than creatinine alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Diabetes, hypertension, glomerular disease, obstruction, recurrent AKI, inherited cystic disease
NSAIDs, smoking and uncontrolled proteinuria accelerate progression

rows.label: Clues
items: Early disease often asymptomatic; advanced disease → fatigue, pruritus, anorexia, edema
Uremia: confusion, myoclonus, pericardial friction rub, nausea or bleeding despite normal platelet count
Labs: normocytic anemia, hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, ↑phosphate, low/normal calcium

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nephron loss → hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, proteinuria and fibrosis
↓Erythropoietin → anemia; phosphate retention/↓calcitriol → ↓calcium absorption → four-gland secondary hyperparathyroidism
Renal bone disease: ↓calcitriol → **deficient osteoid mineralization**, atraumatic fracture; ↑PTH → subperiosteal resorption

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **eGFR <60** or kidney-damage markers for **≥3 months** establishes CKD
Urine albumin/creatinine ratio, urinalysis, creatinine trend; ultrasound for size/obstruction
Stage by GFR and albuminuria; small echogenic kidneys support chronicity but are not universal
Monitor CBC, ferritin/TSAT, K, bicarbonate, calcium, phosphate and PTH

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Albuminuric CKD → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**; monitor creatinine/K; never combine both
SGLT2 inhibitor for T2DM or qualifying albuminuric CKD/HF, generally starting eGFR ≥20
Overload → salt restriction, furosemide; high phosphate → phosphorus restriction, sevelamer; severe hyperparathyroidism → calcitriol
Iron repletion before ESA for selected persistent anemia; correct clinically significant metabolic acidosis
★ **Dialysis (AEIOU)**: refractory acidosis/hyperkalemia/overload (anuria: no diuretics), dialyzable toxins, uremic complications

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiovascular death, fractures, severe hyperkalemic arrhythmia, malnutrition
Dialysis access infection/thrombosis; rapid urea reduction → dialysis disequilibrium
Peritoneal dialysis + fever/abdominal pain → first **peritoneal fluid cell count, Gram stain, culture**

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Preserve arm veins; plan **AV fistula** before hemodialysis; temporary catheter for emergencies; early transplant referral
BP/glycemic control, avoid nephrotoxins, renal drug adjustment; hepatitis B vaccination before dialysis

rows.label: Mimics
items: AKI: acute creatinine change; may complicate established CKD
Prerenal azotemia: reversible perfusion deficit without persistent structural injury

chronic-venous-insufficiency.name: Chronic venous insufficiency
chronic-venous-insufficiency.scope: Varicose veins, stasis dermatitis, venous stasis ulcers, superficial thrombophlebitis, post-thrombotic syndrome
chronic-venous-insufficiency.core: Venous hypertension produces dependent edema, hemosiderin pigmentation, and shallow medial ankle ulcers that improve with elevation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior DVT, obesity, pregnancy, prolonged standing, older age, family history
Reduced calf-muscle pumping from immobility; previous leg trauma or venous surgery

rows.label: Clues
items: Aching/heaviness worsened by standing; varicosities, pitting swelling, preserved pedal pulses
Eczematous itching, lipodermatosclerosis, inverted champagne-bottle leg contour
★ **Irregular, exudative gaiter-region wound**; bilateral erythema without systemic illness favors stasis dermatitis
Superficial thrombophlebitis: focal erythema over a tender palpable venous cord

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Valve failure or outflow obstruction → reflux, capillary leakage, chronic inflammation
Post-thrombotic syndrome: residual obstruction and valvular injury following DVT

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Venous duplex ultrasound** evaluates reflux and obstruction; clinical examination often establishes diagnosis
★ **Ankle-brachial index before compression** when PAD suspected; <0.5 → avoid sustained compression
Nonhealing or atypical ulcer → biopsy for malignancy; sudden unilateral worsening → evaluate acute DVT
New superficial cord → assess clot length, proximity to deep junction, associated DVT

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adequate arterial inflow → **compression bandaging/stockings + leg elevation**; walking activates calf pump
Ulcers: saline cleansing, moist absorbent dressings, debridement when needed
Stasis dermatitis: emollients + short-course topical steroid on intact skin; weeping → saline-soaked dressings, elevation
Symptomatic superficial reflux → endovenous ablation; moderate arterial disease → specialist-guided reduced compression
No antibiotics for colonization alone; cellulitis → systemic antibiotics; no routine diuretics without volume overload

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent ulceration, cellulitis, contact dermatitis; superficial clot can extend into deep veins
Chronic wounds rarely undergo squamous malignant transformation; new growth or bleeding warrants biopsy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight reduction, regular mobility, avoid prolonged dependent posture
Long-term compression after ulcer healing reduces recurrence; moisturize skin and treat venous reflux

rows.label: Mimics
items: Arterial ulcer: painful punched-out toes/lateral ankle, cool foot, weak pulses
Neuropathic ulcer: plantar pressure points, sensory loss, callus
Lymphedema: dorsal foot/toe swelling, later nonpitting thickened skin

table.title: Superficial thrombosis treatment
rows: Short distal segment, no high-risk features
≥5 cm long, >3 cm from deep junction

chronic-venous-insufficiency.evidence: Thrombosis checked 2026-10-30: [SVS/AVF/AVLS 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11523430/); wound care established teaching.

cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.name: Cirrhosis and portal hypertension
cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.scope: Ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatic encephalopathy, esophageal varices, hepatorenal syndrome, hepatocellular carcinoma screening
cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.core: Cirrhosis produces portal hypertension and synthetic failure; new ascites, bleeding, confusion or kidney injury signals decompensation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Alcohol, chronic HBV/HCV, metabolic steatotic liver disease; autoimmune/cholestatic disorders

rows.label: Clues
items: Splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, spider angiomas, jaundice, muscle wasting
Encephalopathy: **asterixis**; triggers GI bleeding, infection, constipation, sedatives, hypokalemia, protein load
SBP may present only with subtle confusion or renal deterioration; fever/pain can be absent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fibrosis raises intrahepatic resistance; splanchnic vasodilation lowers effective arterial volume
Portal collaterals bleed; impaired toxin clearance causes neuropsychiatric dysfunction
SBP: **intestinal bacterial translocation** into ascitic fluid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ New/worsening or hospitalized ascites → **diagnostic paracentesis**; PMN **≥250/µL** → treat SBP
SAAG ≥1.1 g/dL supports portal hypertension; send ascitic culture in bedside blood-culture bottles
HRS-AKI: exclude shock, nephrotoxins, obstruction and structural injury; assess volume response
MELD-Na/MELD 3.0 guides prognosis/transplant assessment
Encephalopathy clinical: **ammonia** not diagnostic; older exam questions may expect serum ammonia after normal head CT

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Variceal bleed → resuscitate, **octreotide + ceftriaxone**, urgent endoscopic banding; refractory → TIPS
Ascites → sodium restriction, spironolactone ± furosemide; tense ascites → paracentesis, albumin if >5 L
★ SBP → **ceftriaxone**, albumin for high-risk renal/liver dysfunction; reassess response
Encephalopathy → lactulose to 2–3 soft stools/day, rifaximin (add for recurrence); correct trigger; no sedatives
HRS → stop diuretics/nephrotoxins, **terlipressin + albumin** after volume assessment; monitor hypoxia; transplant evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: HCC, recurrent infection, malnutrition, hepatopulmonary syndrome; TIPS can worsen encephalopathy
Avoid NSAIDs, sedatives and unnecessary fluid loading; INR alone poorly predicts procedural bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Ultrasound + AFP every 6 months** for HCC surveillance in eligible cirrhosis
Carvedilol for clinically significant portal hypertension when tolerated; banding if indicated and beta blocker unsuitable
After SBP → antibiotic prophylaxis; alcohol abstinence, hepatitis vaccines, adequate protein intake

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cardiac ascites: high SAAG with ascitic protein ≥2.5 g/dL
Malignant/TB ascites: usually low SAAG

colorectal-carcinoma.name: Colorectal carcinoma
colorectal-carcinoma.scope: Colon adenocarcinoma, rectal cancer, staging, surgical resection (hemicolectomy), liver metastases, chemotherapy
colorectal-carcinoma.core: Occult blood loss, altered bowel habits, or obstruction warrants colon evaluation; cancer stage determines local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, adenomas, Lynch/FAP, longstanding colitis, family history; smoking, obesity, processed meat

rows.label: Clues
items: Right-sided lesions → iron-deficiency anemia, fatigue, occult bleeding
Left-sided lesions → constipation, narrowed stools, obstruction; rectal lesions → tenesmus/hematochezia
Weight loss, palpable mass; hepatomegaly or elevated ALP suggests hepatic spread
Bladder invasion → colovesical fistula: fecaluria, mixed fecal flora in urine

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Adenoma–carcinoma sequence involves APC, KRAS, p53; mismatch-repair failure drives microsatellite instability
Portal drainage favors liver metastases; distal rectal tumors may spread directly to lungs

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Colonoscopy with biopsy**; evaluate entire colon for synchronous tumors
★ Confirmed cancer → **CT chest/abdomen/pelvis**, baseline CEA, tumor mismatch-repair/MSI testing
Rectal cancer → pelvic MRI for local staging; CEA cannot diagnose or screen
Obstruction/perforation → urgent contrast CT and surgical assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Resectable colon cancer → **segmental colectomy with lymphadenectomy**; selected liver metastases → resection
Stage III → adjuvant FOLFOX/CAPOX; selected high-risk stage II → individualized chemotherapy
Locally advanced rectal cancer → neoadjuvant systemic chemotherapy/chemoradiation, then total mesorectal excision
Unresectable metastases, nonobstructing primary → **chemotherapy**, no primary resection; MSI-high → checkpoint inhibitor
Perforation or unstable obstruction → urgent operation; selected stable obstruction → stent or diversion

rows.label: Complications
items: Bleeding, perforation, malignant obstruction; venous thrombosis; oxaliplatin neuropathy
Postoperative anastomotic leak; pelvic treatment → urinary/sexual dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Average-risk screening **45–75 years**; earlier colonoscopy for strong family history/hereditary syndromes
Postresection colonoscopy, CEA and stage-based CT surveillance; remove premalignant polyps

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hemorrhoids: outlet bleeding without explanatory anemia; do not dismiss alarm features
IBD: chronic inflammatory diarrhea; diverticulitis: acute focal pain and fever

colorectal-carcinoma.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF colorectal screening](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/colorectal-cancer-screening); treatment: established oncology teaching.

table.title: TNM essentials
rows: Extension through muscle; no regional nodal spread

congenital-heart-disease.name: Congenital heart disease
congenital-heart-disease.scope: Cyanotic heart disease (5 Ts: Tetralogy of Fallot, TGA, truncus, tricuspid atresia, TAPVR), acyanotic heart disease (VSD, ASD, PDA, coarctation of aorta), hyperoxia test, prostaglandin E1
congenital-heart-disease.core: Neonatal cyanosis or shock as the ductus closes demands urgent assessment for duct-dependent congenital heart disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal diabetes, congenital rubella, family history; Down syndrome → AV septal defects
Prematurity → PDA; Turner syndrome → coarctation

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor feeding, diaphoresis, tachypnea, hepatomegaly → infant heart failure
VSD: harsh holosystolic lower-left sternal murmur; ASD: **fixed split S2**, pulmonic flow murmur, RV volume overload
PDA: continuous machinery murmur, bounding pulses; coarctation: weak femoral pulses, arm–leg BP gradient
Central cyanosis: blue lips/tongue, warm extremities → **low arterial saturation**; peripheral: cold extremities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Left-to-right shunts (VSD, ASD, extracardiac PDA) increase pulmonary flow; remodeling can reverse flow → Eisenmenger syndrome
Duct-dependent lesions require pulmonary/systemic flow or mixing through fetal communications
High neonatal PVR limits VSD shunt → murmur appears/louder over weeks as **PVR falls**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Preductal/right-hand and postductal/foot oxygen saturation; **echocardiography** defines anatomy
★ Hyperoxia test: little PaO2 rise with 100% oxygen suggests cardiac shunting; echo preferred
ECG and chest radiograph support diagnosis; normal murmur does not exclude critical disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected duct-dependent lesion → **prostaglandin E1** immediately; monitor for apnea
★ Tet spell (agitation, softer murmur) → knee–chest, oxygen, fluids, morphine; refractory → phenylephrine or propranolol
TGA with inadequate mixing → balloon atrial septostomy, then arterial switch
Large shunts → diuretics, closure; premature PDA → ibuprofen; **obstructed TAPVR → emergency repair**
Coarctation → repair; post-repair paradoxical hypertension → **IV beta-blocker**; Eisenmenger → **do not close shunt**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, failure to thrive, arrhythmias, infective endocarditis
Right-to-left shunting → brain abscess, paradoxical emboli, secondary erythrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pulse-ox newborn screening; rubella immunization before pregnancy; maternal glycemic control
Endocarditis prophylaxis for selected unrepaired cyanotic or prosthetic-material lesions during dental procedures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung disease: substantial oxygen response, pulmonary findings
PPHN: elevated pulmonary resistance with structurally normal heart

table.title: Five cyanotic lesions
rows: RV obstruction, VSD, overriding aorta, RVH; boot-shaped heart
Parallel circuits; single S2; egg-on-string silhouette
Pulmonary veins drain systemically; obstruction → edema

congenital-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric cardiology teaching.

conjunctivitis.name: Conjunctivitis
conjunctivitis.scope: Viral conjunctivitis, bacterial conjunctivitis, allergic conjunctivitis, contact lens-associated keratitis, hygiene and transmission precautions
conjunctivitis.core: A red eye with discharge and preserved vision usually reflects conjunctivitis; significant pain, photophobia, or visual loss requires corneal/ocular evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent respiratory infection, sick contacts, daycare; seasonal allergens and atopy
Contact lenses, poor lens hygiene; sexual exposure with hyperpurulent or persistent disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Gritty sensation, diffuse conjunctival injection; pupils and visual acuity generally normal
★ **Severe pain, photophobia, corneal opacity, reduced vision** → urgent ophthalmology
Copious rapidly recurring pus → gonococcus; chronic follicular disease → chlamydia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Conjunctival inflammation causes vascular dilation and exudate without primary intraocular inflammation
IgE-mediated mast-cell activation drives allergen-associated itching

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Visual acuity first**; inspect pupils, cornea, discharge, preauricular nodes
Fluorescein staining for pain, foreign-body sensation, or lens use; dendrites suggest HSV
Cultures/NAAT for hyperacute purulence, neonatal infection, recurrent or treatment-resistant presentations

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Contact lens use + painful red eye** → remove lenses, urgent keratitis evaluation
Suspected bacterial corneal infection → topical fluoroquinolone with Pseudomonas coverage under ophthalmology
Gonococcal disease → systemic ceftriaxone, irrigation, STI evaluation; topical drops alone insufficient
Chlamydial disease → systemic doxycycline, partner treatment; avoid empiric topical steroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Keratitis, corneal ulceration, scarring; gonococcus can rapidly perforate the cornea
Topical steroid misuse can worsen herpetic infection and raise intraocular pressure

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Handwashing, no shared towels/cosmetics**, avoid eye rubbing; viral disease highly contagious
Discard contaminated lenses/case; avoid swimming or sleeping in lenses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anterior uveitis: consensual photophobia, ciliary flush, cells/flare
Acute angle closure: high IOP, headache/nausea, fixed mid-dilated pupil
Subconjunctival hemorrhage: sharply demarcated blood, no discharge or discomfort; normal vision/exam → **reassurance only**

table.title: Common uncomplicated forms
rows: Watery; URI; preauricular nodes; morning crusting possible

conjunctivitis.evidence: Not checked online; established ophthalmology teaching.

constipation-and-fecal-impaction.name: Constipation and fecal impaction
constipation-and-fecal-impaction.scope: Functional constipation, medication-induced constipation, fecal impaction and overflow incontinence, digital disimpaction, laxatives, fiber
constipation-and-fecal-impaction.core: Difficult, infrequent, or incomplete defecation; loose stool can represent overflow around an impacted rectal stool mass.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low fiber, immobility, dehydration, withholding, older age; childhood onset often follows painful defecation/toilet training
Opioids, anticholinergics, iron, calcium, verapamil; hypothyroidism, hypercalcemia, neurologic disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Hard/lumpy stool, straining, incomplete emptying, <3 spontaneous stools/week; frequency alone insufficient
★ **Rectal fullness, paradoxical diarrhea, fecal soiling, urinary retention** → consider impaction
★ **Bleeding, anemia, weight loss, new persistent change**, severe distension/vomiting → structural evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Slow transit increases water absorption; pelvic-floor dyssynergia prevents coordinated expulsion
Stool retention stretches rectum → reduced sensation and leakage of liquid around retained mass

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ History, drug review, abdominal examination, **digital rectal examination** for stool, masses, pelvic-floor dysfunction
No alarm findings → clinical diagnosis; targeted TSH/calcium if suspected; colonoscopy for alarms or overdue screening
Refractory despite laxatives → anorectal manometry + balloon-expulsion test; then transit studies if needed
Empty rectum does not exclude proximal impaction; obstruction concern → abdominal imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Palpable hard rectal mass → **manual disimpaction**, then enemas; proximal stool → PEG after obstruction excluded
★ Uncomplicated constipation → **fiber gradually + polyethylene glycol**; hydration if depleted, scheduled postmeal toileting
Dyssynergic defecation → pelvic-floor biofeedback; stool softener alone will not correct outlet dysfunction
Opioid-induced: stimulant + osmotic laxative; refractory → naloxegol/naldemedine after excluding bowel obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Anal fissures, hemorrhoids, prolapse, stercoral ulceration/perforation, recurrent impaction
Magnesium laxatives → hypermagnesemia in CKD; phosphate enemas → electrolyte injury, especially renal disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintenance bowel regimen after disimpaction; regular activity, adequate dietary fiber, minimize constipating drugs
Avoid bulk fiber during unresolved impaction; pediatric withholding → reward-based routine, no punishment

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS-C: recurrent abdominal pain related to defecation/stool changes
Bowel obstruction: colicky pain, vomiting, obstipation, dilated bowel
Hirschsprung: neonatal delayed meconium, distension, absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex

table.title: Escalating agents
rows: Limited efficacy; avoid relying on it

constipation-and-fecal-impaction.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA/ACG constipation guideline 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10544839/); impaction and diagnostic pathways established teaching.

contraception.name: Contraception
contraception.scope: Combined oral contraceptives, progestin-only pills, implant, intrauterine devices, tubal sterilization
contraception.core: Choose contraception through shared decisions about efficacy, bleeding, reversibility, adherence, and estrogen-related vascular risk.

rows.label: Who
items: Anyone seeking pregnancy prevention; adolescents and nulliparous patients can use IUDs or implants
Healthy patient: blood pressure suffices; **no pelvic exam** needed before oral contraceptives

rows.label: Schedule
items: Pills daily; depot medroxyprogesterone every 3 months; implants/IUDs last years (product-dependent)
★ Emergency contraception ≤**5 days**: copper IUD/ulipristal; levonorgestrel ≤72 h, no medical contraindications
Progestin-only pills: daily timing crucial; norethindrone less forgiving than drospirenone

rows.label: Special groups
items: Breastfeeding (estrogen lowers milk volume, protein) or estrogen contraindication → progestin-only or copper IUD
Current breast cancer → copper IUD; avoid hormonal methods
Prior VTE, poor adherence → **IUD/implant** (depot raises VTE risk); older exams: depot, avoid IUD after STI

rows.label: Choice
items: Combined pills: suppress ovulation, improve acne/cramps, reduce endometrial/ovarian cancer risk
★ **LARC** minimizes adherence failures; condoms add STI protection
Tubal sterilization: permanent; counsel regret, alternatives, surgical risk, ectopic risk after failure

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Estrogen: **migraine with aura, prior VTE/thrombophilia**, hypertension (stop pill), early postpartum
Smoking age ≥35: combined methods usually avoid; ≥15 cigarettes/day → absolute contraindication
IUD: pregnancy, cervicitis/PID, distorted cavity (non-distorting fibroid OK); copper: also Wilson disease

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Same-day STI screening need not delay insertion without cervicitis; prior PID alone permits IUD
Sterilization: voluntary informed consent; no required partner approval, parity, or marital status
After ulipristal, wait 5 days before progestin; backup contraception needed after hormonal restart

table.title: Long-acting choices
rows: Treats heavy menses; atrophy → expected benign amenorrhea

copd.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
copd.scope: Stable COPD, acute exacerbation (AECOPD), oxygen-induced hypercapnia, noninvasive ventilation (NIV/BiPAP), indications for intubation, bronchodilators and glucocorticoids
copd.core: Persistent airflow obstruction after inhalational exposure causes progressive exertional dyspnea and episodic infectious or inflammatory exacerbations.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Tobacco, biomass smoke, occupational dusts; alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with early/basilar emphysema

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic cough/sputum, prolonged expiration, wheeze, hyperinflation
★ **Somnolence, exhaustion, silent chest, worsening acidosis** → impending respiratory failure
Exacerbation: ↑dyspnea, purulent sputum, rhonchi, **no infiltrate** → acute bronchitis, not pneumonia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Small-airway inflammation + alveolar destruction → expiratory collapse, air trapping, impaired diffusion
Excess oxygen worsens CO₂ retention mainly through V/Q mismatch and Haldane effect

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Postbronchodilator FEV₁/FVC <0.70** confirms persistent obstruction in compatible clinical setting
Exacerbation: pulse oximetry; ABG for severe distress/altered mentation; radiograph for pneumonia, edema, pneumothorax
Consider ECG, troponin, BNP, or PE evaluation when symptoms exceed expected exacerbation pattern

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **albuterol + ipratropium**, prednisone for 5 days; titrate oxygen to 88–92%
Antibiotics: purulence + increased dyspnea/sputum volume, or ventilatory support; doxycycline/azithromycin options
★ Hypercapnic acidosis, pH ≤7.35 → **BiPAP** unless aspiration risk, arrest, instability, inability to cooperate
Intubate for failed NIV, severe encephalopathy, refractory hypoxemia, or inability to protect airway
Long-term oxygen if stable PaO₂ ≤55 or saturation ≤88%; selected cor pulmonale/polycythemia with PaO₂ 56–59

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, secondary polycythemia, cachexia
Pneumonia risk with inhaled steroids; ventilation → dynamic hyperinflation, auto-PEEP, barotrauma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**, influenza/COVID/pneumococcal/RSV vaccination when eligible, pulmonary rehabilitation
Check inhaler technique/adherence; offer alpha-1 antitrypsin testing at least once

rows.label: Mimics
items: Asthma: variable symptoms and reversible obstruction
Heart failure: orthopnea, edema, vascular congestion; bronchiectasis: copious sputum, dilated bronchi

table.title: Stable inhaled treatment
rows: Exacerbations with eosinophilia or concurrent asthma

copd.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [GOLD 2026](https://goldcopd.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/GOLD-REPORT-2026-v1.3-8Dec2025_WMV2.pdf); acute ventilatory care: established teaching.

corneal-abrasion.name: Corneal abrasion
corneal-abrasion.scope: Corneal abrasion, corneal foreign body, fluorescein examination, topical antibiotics, tetanus prophylaxis, chemical eye injury
corneal-abrasion.core: Acute painful red eye after surface trauma; exclude an open globe, retained foreign body, and infectious keratitis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fingernail or plant injury, airborne debris, contact lenses, eye rubbing
High-velocity metalwork suggests intraocular foreign body; alkali exposure penetrates deeply

rows.label: Clues
items: Foreign-body sensation, tearing, photophobia, blepharospasm; vision usually preserved unless central involvement
★ Reduced visual acuity, irregular pupil, hyphema, severe mechanism → urgent ophthalmology
Vertical linear scratches suggest retained material beneath upper eyelid

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Epithelial loss exposes densely innervated cornea; superficial defects generally heal within 24–48 hours
Chemical injury damages epithelium; severe alkali exposure causes stromal and limbal ischemia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Visual acuity → slit-lamp/**fluorescein** examination; evert upper lid for retained particles
Positive Seidel sign: aqueous streaming through fluorescein → open globe; avoid tonometry or manipulation
Suspected intraocular foreign body → orbital CT; avoid MRI if metal possible
Persistent pain beyond expected healing → reassess for ulcer, foreign body, or recurrent erosion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Chemical exposure → immediate copious irrigation; remove particles, continue until stable physiologic pH
Loose surface foreign body → saline irrigation/moistened swab; embedded object or rust ring → trained removal
★ Uncomplicated abrasion → topical **erythromycin**; contact lens-related → ciprofloxacin/ofloxacin for Pseudomonas
Oral NSAID/acetaminophen; no pressure patching or routine take-home topical anesthetic; avoid topical steroids
Open globe → rigid shield, NPO, IV antibiotics, emergency ophthalmology; never remove protruding object

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacterial keratitis, corneal ulcer, scarring, recurrent corneal erosion
Chemical burns: limbal stem-cell loss, corneal melting, glaucoma, permanent visual impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Eye protection; stop contacts until healed; replace contaminated lenses and case
Tetanus prophylaxis: penetrating/contaminated wounds by vaccine history; unnecessary for clean superficial abrasion
Contact lens injury, large/central defect, persistent symptoms → review within 24 hours

rows.label: Mimics
items: HSV keratitis: dendritic fluorescein pattern with terminal bulbs
Corneal ulcer: white stromal infiltrate with epithelial defect
Acute angle closure: fixed mid-dilated pupil, markedly elevated IOP

defense-mechanisms.name: Defense mechanisms
defense-mechanisms.scope: Mature defenses (sublimation, suppression, altruism, humor), neurotic defenses (displacement, rationalization, reaction formation), immature defenses (projection, denial, splitting)
defense-mechanisms.core: Psychological strategies that reduce anxiety from unacceptable feelings or conflict; identify how the original impulse is transformed.

rows.label: Definition
items: Usually unconscious; adaptive value depends on flexibility, context, and consequences
Mature defenses preserve reality testing and constructive functioning

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Sublimation**: unacceptable drive or distress → valued activity; aggression → competitive sports
Altruism: meet personal emotional needs through helping others
Humor: acknowledge painful reality through tolerable amusement

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ **Displacement**: emotion transferred from threatening target to safer target; boss → family
Rationalization: plausible justification conceals true motive; rejection blamed on disliking the job
Reaction formation: impulse → exaggerated opposite behavior; hostility → excessive kindness

rows.label: Compare
items: ★ **Projection**: own unacceptable feeling attributed to another; unfaithful partner accuses spouse
Denial: refusal to acknowledge external reality despite evidence
★ **Splitting**: people classified entirely good or bad; alternating idealization and devaluation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Suppression**: conscious postponement; repression: unconscious exclusion from awareness
Intentional lying for external benefit → malingering, not denial
One immature defense alone ≠ personality disorder; assess persistent, pervasive pattern

defense-mechanisms.evidence: Established psychiatric definitions; no treatment guideline involved.

depressive-disorders.name: Depressive disorders
depressive-disorders.scope: Major depressive disorder criteria, depression in older adults, bereavement vs MDD, pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, suicide risk
depressive-disorders.core: Persistent low mood or loss of pleasure with neurovegetative and cognitive symptoms, causing clinically significant distress or impaired function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior episodes, family history, chronic illness/pain, substance use, postpartum period, social isolation
Older adults: disability, bereavement, polypharmacy; somatic presentations

rows.label: Clues
items: SIGECAPS: sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor change, suicidality
Psychotic depression: delusions/hallucinations only during mood episodes, often guilt or nihilism
★ **Suicide risk**: prior attempt, intent, plan, means, agitation, psychosis, intoxication
Youth: **irritable mood** qualifies; academic decline, withdrawal, somatic complaints; not normal teenage behavior

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial mood-circuit dysfunction involving monoamines, **HPA hyperactivity with raised cortisol**, and neuroplasticity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ MDD: **≥5 symptoms for ≥2 weeks**, including depressed mood or anhedonia; exclude mania/hypomania
Screen all adults, even asymptomatic: PHQ-2, PHQ-9 for severity; older adults: **Geriatric Depression Scale**
Interview establishes diagnosis; assess substances, drugs, TSH/CBC when clinically suspected
★ **Ask directly about suicide**, access to firearms, protective factors; questioning does not increase risk
Post-CABG anhedonia, withdrawal, fatigue → depression screen; vein-harvest leg edema expected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Imminent danger or **severe malnutrition** → **observation, psychiatric hospitalization**; remove lethal means
Mild: CBT/interpersonal therapy; moderate/severe: sertraline + psychotherapy; pregnancy → shared risk–benefit discussion
★ Urgent suicidality/catatonia/anorexia → **ECT**; psychotic depression → ECT or antidepressant + antipsychotic
Alternatives: **bupropion** (fatigue/hypersomnia, smoking cessation), **mirtazapine** (poor appetite, insomnia)
Continue antidepressant ≥6 months after remission; recurrent/severe episodes → longer maintenance

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, malnutrition, functional decline, recurrence
SSRIs: sexual dysfunction, GI effects, hyponatremia; early activation/suicidality monitoring, especially age <25
Bupropion: seizures; avoid with eating disorders, seizure disorders or brain tumor; mirtazapine: weight gain/sedation
Benzodiazepines in older adults: worsen depression, sedation, falls → stop, use antidepressant

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safety plan, early follow-up after drug changes
Taper antidepressants to reduce discontinuation symptoms; avoid antidepressant monotherapy in bipolar disorder

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dementia: insidious consistent deficits; **pseudodementia**: subacute, "I don't know" answers, recall improves with prompting
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, constipation, elevated TSH
Untreated OSA: snoring, obesity, sleepiness → **mood disorder due to medical condition**, not MDD
Anorexia nervosa: fear of weight gain, distorted body image

table.title: Distinguishing persistent sadness
rows: Waves tied to reminders; self-esteem usually preserved
Pervasive worthlessness; bereavement does not exclude diagnosis
Stressor within 3 months; MDD criteria absent

dermatophyte-infections.name: Dermatophyte infections
dermatophyte-infections.scope: Tinea capitis, tinea corporis, tinea pedis, tinea cruris, onychomycosis, potassium hydroxide preparation, oral and topical antifungals
dermatophyte-infections.core: Keratin-invading fungi cause scaly skin lesions or infected hair/nails; the anatomic site determines topical versus systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Warm humid conditions, occlusive footwear, shared showers, wrestling, infected animals or contacts
Diabetes, immunosuppression; childhood favors scalp infection; nail disease increases with age

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus and peripheral scaling; steroid exposure may distort borders and suppress inflammation
★ **Boggy tender scalp plaque** → kerion; inflammatory disease risks permanent scarring alopecia
Interdigital maceration/fissures can become bacterial entry sites

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton digest keratin in stratum corneum, hair, and nails
**T rubrum** most common on skin/nails; capitis → **T tonsurans** (endothrix)
Follicular/deep involvement prevents topical agents from reaching the infected reservoir

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **KOH preparation of active edge** → branching septate hyphae; obtain before systemic treatment when uncertain
Scalp: hair/plucked scale microscopy and culture; nail: clipping KOH, PAS, or fungal culture
Wood lamp detects only selected organisms; negative fluorescence does not exclude tinea
Refractory/widespread infection → reassess diagnosis, adherence, resistance; fungal culture can guide further care

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Limited skin disease → **topical terbinafine** or clotrimazole; continue beyond clinical clearing
★ Hair infection → **oral griseofulvin or terbinafine**; adjunct selenium sulfide/ketoconazole shampoo reduces spread
Nail infection → confirm fungus, then oral terbinafine; baseline liver assessment; counsel slow regrowth
Avoid topical corticosteroid monotherapy or steroid-antifungal combinations; extensive disease may require oral antifungal

rows.label: Complications
items: Secondary cellulitis, persistent nail dystrophy, recurrent infection from untreated reservoirs
Oral antifungals: hepatotoxicity, drug interactions; griseofulvin contraindicated during pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Keep feet dry**, change socks, avoid shared towels/combs, disinfect sports gear
Treat symptomatic contacts/pets and coexisting tinea pedis (autoinfects groin → recurrence); avoid barefoot communal-shower exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Candida intertrigo: satellite pustules, scrotal involvement
Psoriasis: sharply demarcated plaques, nail pitting; alopecia areata: smooth nonscaly patches

table.title: Site clues
rows: Broken hairs, black dots, patchy alopecia, occipital nodes
Annular plaque, advancing border, central clearing
Thick yellow brittle nail, subungual debris

dermatophyte-infections.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatophyte diagnosis and site-based treatment.

diagnostic-test-accuracy.name: Diagnostic test accuracy
diagnostic-test-accuracy.scope: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios, cut-off changes
diagnostic-test-accuracy.core: Diagnostic accuracy: classification performance against a reference standard; distinguish detection ability from the probability that a result reflects disease.

rows.label: Definition
items: TP/FP: diseased/nondiseased testing positive; FN/TN: diseased/nondiseased testing negative
False negatives → low sensitivity, an intrinsic test property; NPV varies with prevalence

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ ↑Prevalence → **↑PPV, ↓NPV**; sensitivity/specificity unchanged if disease spectrum unchanged
★ Positive above threshold: **lower cutoff → ↑sensitivity, ↓specificity**; raising cutoff reverses
LR+ >10 rules in; LR− <0.1 rules out; **LR 1** → no information

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Pretest odds = p/(1−p); **posttest odds = pretest odds × LR**
Posttest probability = odds/(1+odds); pretest 20%, LR+ 4 → odds 1 → 50%
Parallel tests, either positive → ↑sensitivity; serial tests, both positive → ↑specificity

rows.label: Compare
items: ROC: sensitivity versus 1−specificity; AUC 0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect
ROC point nearest **upper-left corner** → best combined sensitivity and specificity

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Sensitive negative** helps exclude; specific positive helps confirm; neither absolute
Case-control sampling → PPV/NPV unrepresentative without population prevalence
Verification bias: reference testing only selected results → distorted accuracy

diagnostic-test-accuracy.evidence: Established statistical definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

disruptive-behavior-disorders.name: Disruptive behavior disorders
disruptive-behavior-disorders.scope: Oppositional defiant disorder (ODD), conduct disorder (CD, aggression, property destruction, rule violations, ASPD precursor), intermittent explosive disorder, parent management training, family therapy
disruptive-behavior-disorders.core: Differentiate persistent defiance, violations of others’ rights, and brief impulsive aggressive outbursts; family and behavioral interventions anchor treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family conflict, inconsistent or harsh discipline, trauma, parental psychopathology, antisocial peers
ADHD, learning disorders, substance use can worsen behavioral dysregulation

rows.label: Clues
items: Assess aggression toward people/animals, deliberate fire-setting, theft, truancy, and running away
Callous-unemotional traits: limited remorse/empathy and shallow affect; poorer conduct-disorder prognosis
★ **Planned aggression for material gain** argues against intermittent explosive disorder

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Temperamental impulse-control vulnerability interacts with reinforcing family, peer and environmental patterns

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Multi-informant assessment**: caregivers, child, school; developmental context and functioning across settings
ODD: ≥4 symptoms; interaction with ≥1 nonsibling; frequency beyond developmental expectations
CD: ≥3 qualifying behaviors in 12 months, ≥1 in last 6 months
IED: impulsive disproportionate outbursts; age ≥6; twice weekly for 3 months or three destructive episodes/year

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Parent management training**, consistent reinforcement and consequences; family and school collaboration
Adolescent CD: multimodal/multisystemic family interventions; address safety and peer environment
★ Treat comorbid ADHD with stimulants when diagnosed; medication not routine for ODD/CD alone
Danger to others → **inpatient psychiatric admission**; refractory aggression → short-term risperidone, metabolic monitoring
IED: CBT for impulse/anger control; selected cases → fluoxetine

rows.label: Complications
items: Academic failure, family disruption, injury, legal problems, substance use
CD may precede antisocial personality disorder; adult diagnosis requires age ≥18 and CD evidence before 15

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early parenting support, trauma-informed care, learning accommodations, stable supervision and positive school supports

rows.label: Mimics
items: DMDD: persistent between-outburst irritability, onset before age 10
Bipolar disorder: distinct manic episodes with decreased need for sleep
ADHD: impulsive noncompliance without deliberate rights violations

table.title: Core distinction
rows: ≥6 months angry/argumentative/vindictive; no major rights violations
Aggression, destruction, deceit/theft, serious rule violations

dyslipidemia.name: Dyslipidemia
dyslipidemia.scope: Lipid screening guidelines, ASCVD risk calculation, statin therapy indications, monitoring response to diet and pharmacotherapy
dyslipidemia.core: Excess atherogenic lipoproteins drive ASCVD; treatment intensity follows established disease, severe LDL elevation, diabetes, and estimated absolute cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Familial disorders, saturated-fat intake, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis
Premature ASCVD family history, CKD, smoking, inflammatory disease increase treatment benefit

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; tendon xanthomas/early corneal arcus suggest familial hypercholesterolemia
Severe triglyceride elevation: eruptive xanthomas, pancreatitis; low HDL alone is not a drug target

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retained apoB-containing particles → arterial inflammation and plaque formation
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation
Familial hypercholesterolemia: **defective LDL-receptor uptake** → isolated high LDL, clear plasma; high TG: milky plasma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Lipid panel from age 19, at least every 5 years**; earlier/more often with risk
Nonfasting panel acceptable; markedly high triglycerides → fasting repeat/secondary-cause evaluation; Lp(a) once/lifetime
★ **PREVENT-ASCVD**, ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 without ASCVD: replaces pooled-cohort equations in 2026 guidance
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium; zero insufficient for deferral with diabetes, smoking, strong premature history
High total cholesterol alone → full lipid panel before treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinical ASCVD (CAD, stroke, PAD) or **LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin**, no risk calculation required
★ Diabetes age 40–75 → **at least moderate-intensity statin**; multiple risk factors favor high intensity
Above LDL target despite maximal statin → ezetimibe; consider PCSK9 inhibitor or bempedoic acid
Severe triglycerides ≥500 → address causes, diet, consider fenofibrate/prescription omega-3 to reduce pancreatitis risk
Adolescent obesity + moderate LDL → **calorie reduction/lifestyle first**; statin only if severe or persistent

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, stroke, peripheral arterial disease; statins → myalgias, rare rhabdomyolysis, small diabetes-risk increase
Baseline ALT; CK only with symptoms/risk; most lipid-lowering drugs deferred during conception/pregnancy/lactation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mediterranean-style diet, replace saturated fats, exercise, weight reduction, smoking cessation
★ Recheck lipids **4–12 weeks after diet/drug change**, then every 3–12 months; high despite diet → statin
High intensity lowers LDL ≥50%: atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypothyroidism: elevated TSH; correct before labeling primary dyslipidemia
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia; treat renal cause

table.title: Risk-based primary prevention and secondary target

early-pregnancy-loss.name: Early pregnancy loss
early-pregnancy-loss.scope: Threatened abortion, inevitable abortion, incomplete abortion, complete abortion, missed abortion, anembryonic pregnancy
early-pregnancy-loss.core: First-trimester bleeding requires pregnancy location and viability assessment before labeling miscarriage or choosing expectant, medical, or surgical management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Embryonic aneuploidy most common; maternal age, prior losses, uterine anomalies, antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Clues
items: Cramping, vaginal bleeding, passage of tissue; symptoms may be absent with retained nonviable pregnancy
★ Hypotension, syncope, peritoneal signs → **hemorrhage or ruptured ectopic**
Fever, uterine tenderness, foul discharge → septic abortion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryonic/fetal demise or failed embryonic development → decidual separation and variable cervical dilation
Corpus luteum progesterone sustains pregnancy until ~10 weeks; removal earlier → **progesterone supplementation**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** plus quantitative β-hCG; CBC, blood type, pelvic examination
Definitive nonviability: CRL ≥7 mm without heartbeat or mean sac diameter ≥25 mm without embryo
Absent embryo/heartbeat on repeat: ≥11 days after yolk sac, ≥14 days after sac-only → nonviable
No intrauterine pregnancy → serial hCG/ultrasound; tissue passage alone cannot exclude ectopic

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable, infected, or uncontrolled hemorrhage → **urgent uterine aspiration**; sepsis → IV broad-spectrum antibiotics
Confirmed stable loss → patient choice: observation, mifepristone followed by misoprostol, or aspiration
Threatened loss → expectant follow-up; bed rest does not prevent miscarriage
Stable, unlocated pregnancy, falling hCG → serial hCG until negative; no methotrexate
★ Rh-negative loss **≥12 weeks → RhIg**; ACOG omits routine testing earlier; older exam questions may expect Rh typing

rows.label: Complications
items: Retained products, infection, hemorrhage; intrauterine adhesions after instrumentation; grief/depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking/alcohol avoidance, optimize diabetes; most isolated chromosomal losses unpreventable
Recurrent clinical losses → assess uterine anatomy, antiphospholipid antibodies and selected genetic causes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine implantation, adnexal mass/free fluid
Gestational trophoblastic disease: very high hCG, abnormal cystic intrauterine tissue
Subchorionic hematoma: bleeding without cramping; viable intrauterine pregnancy, perichorionic collection
Normal early pregnancy: spotting, 5-week sac, hCG ~1,000, simple corpus luteum cyst; embryo not yet expected

encephalitis.name: Encephalitis
encephalitis.scope: Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1), temporal lobe lesions, CSF analysis (elevated RBCs, lymphocytic pleocytosis, PCR), IV acyclovir, West Nile virus, autoimmune encephalitis
encephalitis.core: Fever with sustained altered mental status, seizures, or focal neurologic deficits suggests brain inflammation and warrants immediate empiric acyclovir.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HSV-1 often occurs without immunosuppression; mosquito exposure suggests arboviruses
Autoimmune disease or tumor association; anti-NMDA receptor disease sometimes accompanies ovarian teratoma
Neonate, days–weeks old: perinatal HSV → seizures, fever, CSF RBCs, negative Gram stain

rows.label: Clues
items: HSV: personality change, aphasia, olfactory hallucinations, focal seizures
★ **Temporal lobe abnormalities** strongly suggest HSV; hemorrhagic CSF possible but not required
West Nile: movement disorder or asymmetric flaccid weakness; anti-NMDA: psychosis, dyskinesia, autonomic instability
Paraneoplastic limbic: **small cell lung cancer**, subacute psychosis/memory loss, medial temporal lesions, negative HSV PCR

rows.label: Pathophys
items: HSV causes necrotizing inflammation, often limbic/temporal; mosquito-borne viruses infect neuronal tissue
Autoantibodies against neuronal surface antigens disrupt synaptic signaling

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **LP: CSF cells, protein, glucose, HSV PCR**; lymphocytes, ↑protein, usually normal glucose
Neuroimaging before LP for focal deficits, papilledema, marked impaired consciousness, or suspected mass effect
MRI more sensitive than CT; EEG identifies nonconvulsive seizures or temporal periodic discharges
Early negative PCR with strong suspicion → continue treatment and repeat CSF PCR in 3–7 days
West Nile: CSF IgM; autoimmune suspicion → CSF/serum antibodies and tumor search

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected HSV → **IV acyclovir immediately**, usually 14–21 days; do not await PCR
Airway/seizure support; possible bacterial infection → ceftriaxone + vancomycin; Listeria risk → add ampicillin
Acyclovir: renal adjustment, IV hydration; West Nile: supportive care
★ Autoimmune disease → **steroids, IVIG/plasma exchange**, tumor removal after infectious evaluation
Reduced consciousness, status epilepticus, or respiratory compromise → ICU-level care

rows.label: Complications
items: Persistent memory impairment, epilepsy, focal deficits, death; acyclovir crystal nephropathy
Severe autoimmune disease: arrhythmia, hypoventilation, prolonged rehabilitation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mosquito repellent, protective clothing, vector control; no routine HSV encephalitis vaccine

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bacterial meningitis: neutrophilic CSF, low glucose; overlap requires empiric coverage
Toxic/metabolic delirium: systemic explanation without inflammatory CSF
Primary psychosis: lacks new seizures, dysautonomia, or focal neurologic abnormalities
Rabies: animal/bat exposure, **hydrophobia**, hypersalivation, agitation

encephalitis.evidence: Not checked online; established infectious and autoimmune neurology teaching.

esophageal-motility-disorders.name: Esophageal motility disorders
esophageal-motility-disorders.scope: Achalasia, diffuse esophageal spasm, hypercontractile esophagus, Zenker diverticulum, manometry, barium swallow
esophageal-motility-disorders.core: Dysphagia to solids and liquids from onset suggests impaired motility; progressive solids-first dysphagia suggests mechanical obstruction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Achalasia often idiopathic; Chagas disease can destroy enteric ganglia
Older age predisposes to Zenker diverticulum; opioids can produce spastic motility patterns

rows.label: Clues
items: Achalasia: regurgitated undigested food, nocturnal cough, weight loss
★ Zenker: **halitosis, cervical gurgling, aspiration**, retained food hours after eating
Spastic disorders: intermittent dysphagia and squeezing chest pain; hot/cold liquids may provoke

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Achalasia: loss of inhibitory myenteric neurons → impaired LES relaxation and absent peristalsis
Zenker: cricopharyngeal dysfunction → mucosal herniation through Killian triangle

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Esophageal symptoms → **upper endoscopy** to exclude stricture/cancer before motility testing
★ **High-resolution manometry** confirms functional disorder after structural disease excluded
Barium swallow defines emptying; suspected Zenker → **barium study before endoscopy**
Rapid weight loss, older onset or difficult LES passage → evaluate pseudoachalasia with CT/endoscopic ultrasound
Chest pain → exclude ACS before labeling esophageal spasm

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Achalasia → pneumatic dilation, Heller myotomy + fundoplication, or **POEM**
Botulinum toxin for achalasia when procedural risk precludes durable treatment
Spastic disorders → remove opioid trigger, treat reflux; diltiazem or nitrates for persistent symptoms
Symptomatic Zenker → **cricopharyngeal myotomy + diverticulectomy** or endoscopic septotomy; no dilation or blind NG tube

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration pneumonia, malnutrition; longstanding achalasia → increased squamous cancer risk
Dilation/myotomy → perforation; myotomy, especially POEM → gastroesophageal reflux

rows.label: Prevention
items: Eat slowly, chew thoroughly, remain upright after meals to reduce regurgitation/aspiration

rows.label: Mimics
items: Esophageal cancer: progressive solids-first symptoms; obstructing lesion
Scleroderma: hypotensive LES with reflux, distal aperistalsis

table.title: Manometry and contrast findings
rows: Impaired LES relaxation; absent normal peristalsis

esophageal-motility-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACG achalasia guideline](https://gi.org/guideline/diagnosis-and-management-of-achalasia/); other disorders established teaching.

essential-hypertension.name: Essential hypertension
essential-hypertension.scope: Blood pressure staging, nonpharmacologic interventions (weight loss, DASH, exercise), first-line antihypertensive agents, resistant hypertension
essential-hypertension.core: Persistently elevated arterial pressure usually reflects multifactorial primary hypertension; confirm accurate repeated measurements before long-term treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, family history, obesity, excess sodium/alcohol, inactivity, poor sleep
NSAIDs, stimulants, oral contraceptives can raise BP; assess before labeling primary disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; headache alone does not establish hypertensive emergency
★ **Acute target-organ injury** with severe pressure → hypertensive emergency; BP number alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased vascular resistance, altered renal sodium handling, sympathetic/RAAS activation sustain elevated pressure
Chronic endothelial injury accelerates atherosclerosis and small-vessel organ damage
Older adults: large-artery stiffness (low compliance) → **isolated systolic hypertension**, wide pulse pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Average ≥2 readings on ≥2 visits; confirm using **home BP or ambulatory monitoring**
Rest seated, feet supported, correct cuff, arm at heart level; avoid recent caffeine/exercise
BMP, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis/albuminuria, lipids, glucose/A1c, ECG assess risk and injury
Resistant: above goal on 3 agents including diuretic, or controlled on ≥4; exclude pseudoresistance
Child/adolescent high oscillometric reading → **confirm by auscultation** before ambulatory monitoring or workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **DASH diet, weight reduction, sodium restriction, aerobic activity**, moderate alcohol; target generally <130/80
≥140/90 → drugs, usually two classes; ≥130/80 with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT ≥7.5% → drugs
★ Low-risk stage 1: **3–6 months lifestyle**, then drugs if still ≥130/80; updated 2025 threshold
Initial: chlorthalidone, amlodipine, lisinopril, or losartan; albuminuric CKD → ACE inhibitor/ARB (older exams: any diabetes)
Resistant after optimized triple regimen → spironolactone; monitor K/creatinine; never combine ACE inhibitor + ARB

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, LV hypertrophy/HF, CKD, retinopathy, aortic disease
Thiazide: low Na/K, gout; ACE inhibitor: cough/angioedema; RAAS drugs contraindicated in pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication adherence, home readings, regular follow-up; assess orthostatic symptoms in older adults
Weight loss: largest lifestyle BP drop, ~1 mm Hg/kg; smoking cessation barely lowers resting BP
BP control: largest modifiable stroke-risk reduction; also prevents concentric LVH and HF

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: office high, home normal
Masked hypertension: elevated out-of-office only; secondary causes: abrupt/refractory pressure with renal/endocrine clues

extremity-vascular-injury.name: Extremity vascular injury
extremity-vascular-injury.scope: Hard signs (pulsatile bleeding, expanding hematoma, absent pulses, thrill/bruit, pallor), soft signs (diminished pulse, proximity), surgical exploration vs CT angiography
extremity-vascular-injury.core: After limb trauma, active arterial bleeding or threatened perfusion requires immediate intervention; stable equivocal findings require objective vascular assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Penetrating wounds near major vessels; blunt crush or traction injury
Knee dislocation, supracondylar humeral fracture, open fractures; spontaneous joint reduction may conceal mechanism

rows.label: Clues
items: Pain, pallor, coolness, paresthesia, paralysis indicate worsening ischemia; motor deficit is late
★ **Normal distal pulses do not exclude injury**, especially intimal tears after knee dislocation
Examine both limbs and document pulses, motor function, sensation before and after reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transection causes hemorrhage; intimal disruption → thrombosis and delayed ischemia
Contained arterial leak → pseudoaneurysm; artery–vein communication → traumatic AV fistula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Hard signs → immediate **operative exploration**; imaging must not delay limb-saving treatment
Stable without hard signs → ABI/API; **<0.9** or abnormal examination → CT angiography
Normal examination + index ≥0.9 → serial examinations/follow-up; observe high-risk blunt injuries
Duplex ultrasound alternative in selected stable patients; CTA localizes injury for repair

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Direct pressure; uncontrolled hemorrhage → proximal tourniquet; avoid blind clamping
Resuscitate hemorrhagic shock with blood products; urgent vascular surgery consultation
★ Restore arterial flow rapidly, ideally within 6 hours; primary repair or vein graft
Temporary shunt when definitive repair delayed; coordinate fracture stabilization and revascularization
Prolonged ischemia, crush injury, marked swelling → early fasciotomy; monitor reperfusion hyperkalemia

rows.label: Complications
items: Amputation, persistent neuropathy, compartment syndrome; rhabdomyolysis and AKI after reperfusion
Delayed thrombosis, pseudoaneurysm, AV fistula, graft infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Repeat neurovascular checks after splinting, reduction, and repair; promptly loosen constrictive dressings
Discharge follow-up essential for delayed swelling, recurrent bleeding, bruit, or new ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Compartment syndrome: pain with passive stretch, tense compartments; pulses often remain palpable
Isolated nerve injury: focal deficits without objective perfusion abnormality

table.title: Trauma signs
rows: Absent pulses; bruit/thrill; overt distal ischemia
Diminished pulse; stable hematoma; prior bleeding

foreign-body-aspiration.name: Foreign body aspiration
foreign-body-aspiration.scope: Pediatric airway foreign body, choking maneuvers, rigid bronchoscopy, chest x-ray findings (air trapping, atelectasis), observation of partial obstruction
foreign-body-aspiration.core: Abrupt choking with unilateral wheeze or reduced breath sounds in a toddler suggests airway foreign body, even with normal radiographs.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Children <3 years exploring objects orally; nuts, seeds, grapes, hot dogs, toy fragments
Neurologic swallowing impairment, sedation, intoxication, poor dentition in adults

rows.label: Clues
items: Witnessed coughing/gagging during eating or play; symptoms may partially resolve after initial event
★ **Cannot speak, cough effectively, or breathe** → severe airway obstruction
Proximal obstruction: stridor; distal obstruction: focal wheeze, persistent cough, recurrent same-lobe pneumonia
Cyanosis, altered consciousness, exhaustion → imminent respiratory arrest

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Partial ball-valve blockage allows inspiration but limits expiration → distal hyperinflation
Complete bronchial blockage → resorption atelectasis; retained organic material causes inflammation and infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable child → **chest x-ray**, including expiratory or bilateral decubitus views when feasible
Unilateral air trapping, mediastinal shift, collapse, or radiopaque object may identify location
Most food objects are radiolucent; negative examination/imaging does not exclude a convincing history
★ High suspicion → **bronchoscopy**; avoid delaying definitive evaluation for repeated imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: Effective cough/partial obstruction → encourage coughing, observe closely; no blind finger sweep
★ Infant severe choking: **5 back blows + 5 chest thrusts**, repeat
Age ≥1 year: cycles of five back blows/five abdominal thrusts; pregnancy/marked obesity → chest thrusts
