Short-bowel syndrome after extensive resection; reperfusion injury, recurrent thrombosis
Ischemic colitis can heal with segmental stricture

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Anticoagulate AF when eligible**; smoking cessation, statin, atherosclerotic risk reduction
Treat low-flow triggers promptly; thrombophilia evaluation for selected venous thrombosis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infectious colitis: exposure/fever, stool pathogen identification
Pancreatitis: epigastric/back pain with lipase elevation
Perforated viscus: early rigid abdomen/free air; bowel obstruction: transition point on CT
Aortoenteric fistula: months-years after aortic graft, herald then massive upper GI bleed

table.title: Chronic disease versus colonic ischemia
rows: Postprandial pain, food fear, weight loss
Cramps then hematochezia; older, low-flow, post-AAA repair
Fluids, bowel rest; ceftriaxone/metronidazole if moderate/severe

mesenteric-ischemia.evidence: Colonic disease checked 2026-10-30: [ACG colon ischemia guideline](https://acgcdn.gi.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/ACG-Colon-Ischemia-Guideline-Summary.pdf); acute mesenteric treatment: established emergency framework.

multiple-myeloma.name: Multiple myeloma
multiple-myeloma.scope: CRAB features (hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, bone lytic lesions), SPEP/UPEP M-spike, serum free light chains, bone marrow biopsy (>10% plasma cells), MGUS, smoldering myeloma
multiple-myeloma.core: A clonal plasma-cell malignancy causes monoclonal protein production and organ damage; modern biomarkers can establish treatment-requiring disease before symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, Black ancestry, male sex, preexisting MGUS; usually no identifiable preventable exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **CRAB**: hypercalcemia, renal impairment, anemia, lytic bone lesions
Back/rib pain, pathologic fracture, recurrent bacterial infection, high total protein, rouleaux
Acute weakness/back pain → cord compression; proteinuria or restrictive cardiomyopathy → consider AL amyloid

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Marrow expansion suppresses blood formation; osteoclast activation without osteoblast response causes bone destruction
Light chains injure renal tubules; low polyclonal immunoglobulins → **encapsulated bacteria**, e.g., pneumococcus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **SPEP/immunofixation + free light chains**, urine studies; light-chain disease may lack serum spike
★ **Bone marrow biopsy** quantifies clonal plasma cells; whole-body low-dose CT/MRI assesses bone disease
Active disease: ≥10% clonal marrow cells/plasmacytoma plus attributable CRAB or myeloma-defining biomarker
SLiM: marrow ≥60%; involved/uninvolved FLC ratio ≥100 with involved FLC ≥100 mg/L
MRI >1 focal lesion ≥5 mm defines active disease; bone scan may miss lytic lesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Bortezomib-based combination** ± daratumumab/lenalidomide/dexamethasone; selected patients → autologous transplant
Hypercalcemia → saline plus antiresorptive; AKI → hydration, avoid NSAIDs/contrast and rapidly reduce light chains
Cord compression → dexamethasone and urgent MRI/radiation or surgery; treat infections promptly
MGUS/smoldering disease generally monitored; high-risk smoldering disease merits specialist assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Cast nephropathy, vertebral collapse, hyperviscosity, AL amyloidosis; treatment-related neuropathy, infections and thrombosis
Urine dipstick detects albumin, misses light chains; negative dipstick does not exclude cast nephropathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccines, bisphosphonates; proteasome inhibitors → antiviral prophylaxis; immunomodulators → thromboprophylaxis by risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Metastatic carcinoma: destructive lesions without clonal plasma-cell findings
Waldenström macroglobulinemia: IgM, hyperviscosity/lymphadenopathy, usually no lytic lesions

multiple-myeloma.evidence: Criteria checked 2026-10-30: [IMWG diagnostic criteria](https://www.myeloma.org/newly-diagnosed/multiple-myeloma-diagnostic-criteria); treatment: established generalist teaching.

multiple-sclerosis.name: Multiple sclerosis
multiple-sclerosis.scope: Relapsing-remitting, optic neuritis, transverse myelitis, internuclear ophthalmoplegia (MLF lesion), Uhthoff phenomenon, Lhermitte sign, disease-modifying therapies
multiple-sclerosis.core: Neurologic deficits separated in location and time, often including optic neuritis, suggest inflammatory CNS demyelination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young adulthood, female sex, **Northern European ancestry**, family history; EBV, smoking, low vitamin D

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Optic neuritis: **pain with eye movement**, monocular loss, poor color vision, afferent pupillary defect, often normal fundus
Internuclear ophthalmoplegia: **MLF lesion**, impaired ipsilateral adduction, contralateral abducting nystagmus; convergence intact
Uhthoff: old deficits worsen with heat; Lhermitte: neck flexion triggers electric spinal sensation
Transverse myelitis: weakness, sensory level, urinary dysfunction; acute relapse generally lasts >24 hours

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-mediated oligodendrocyte/myelin injury → CNS plaques, conduction block and eventual axonal loss
Relapsing-remitting: attacks with recovery; progressive forms: accumulating disability between or without attacks

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **MRI brain/cord**: periventricular, cortical/juxtacortical, infratentorial, spinal lesions; 2024 criteria add optic nerve
Classic time dissemination: new follow-up lesion or simultaneous enhancing/nonenhancing lesions; exclude better explanation
CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands support diagnosis; revised criteria also accept kappa free-light-chain index
Atypical severe visual loss/long cord lesion → serum AQP4/MOG antibodies; revised criteria permit selected earlier diagnoses
Suspected relapse → exclude fever, UTI and metabolic triggers before escalating immunosuppression

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Disabling relapse/optic neuritis → **high-dose IV methylprednisolone**, not low-dose prednisone; refractory → plasma exchange
★ Relapsing disease → early disease-modifying drug, e.g., **ocrelizumab**, tailored to activity and pregnancy plans
Lower-activity options include interferon-beta or glatiramer; natalizumab requires JC-virus/PML risk assessment
Baclofen for spasticity; rehabilitation, bladder care and treatment of neuropathic pain
Isolated heat/infection-related worsening → treat trigger; not automatically a new inflammatory attack

rows.label: Complications
items: Gait impairment, falls, neurogenic bladder, depression and cognitive dysfunction
Immunosuppressive treatment → infection; some agents carry PML risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, exercise, vaccination; review contraception/pregnancy before disease-modifying drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: B12 deficiency: symmetric posterior-column dysfunction, macrocytosis
NMOSD: AQP4-positive, often severe attacks; some MS drugs worsen disease
Stroke: abrupt maximal deficit, vascular territory

neural-tube-defects.name: Neural tube defects
neural-tube-defects.scope: Anencephaly, spina bifida occulta, meningocele, myelomeningocele, Chiari II malformation, maternal serum AFP, amniotic acetylcholinesterase, lemon and banana signs, folic acid prevention
neural-tube-defects.core: Neural tube closure failure by approximately 4 weeks after conception produces cranial or spinal defects; prevention must begin before pregnancy recognition.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low folate, prior affected pregnancy, maternal diabetes/obesity, valproate/carbamazepine, early-pregnancy hyperthermia

rows.label: Clues
items: Midline lumbosacral sac, lower-limb weakness, absent reflexes, bladder dysfunction with neural involvement
★ **Lemon skull and banana cerebellum** on fetal ultrasound suggest open spina bifida/Chiari II
Occult lesions: hair tuft, atypical deep dimple, hemangioma; normal skin does not guarantee normal cord

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failed neurulation leaves neural tissue unprotected; CSF leakage contributes to hindbrain herniation
Folate supports nucleotide synthesis during rapid embryonic cell division

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal serum **AFP at 15–22 weeks**; elevation → verify dating/number, detailed ultrasound
Open defects elevate AFP; closed occulta may not; cfDNA does not screen neural tube defects
★ Uncertain imaging → amniotic fluid **AFP and acetylcholinesterase**; target anatomy scan at 18–22 weeks
Postnatal spinal ultrasound in young infant or MRI for suspected occult dysraphism/tethered cord

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Open spinal lesion: **prone positioning, sterile saline dressing**, avoid pressure/contamination; neonatal neurosurgery
Early closure; assess hydrocephalus, renal function and bladder emptying; intermittent catheterization when neurogenic
Selected prenatal myelomeningocele repair can improve motor outcomes/reduce shunting, with maternal and prematurity risks
Anencephaly → counseling, pregnancy options, and palliative neonatal care; no curative treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Hydrocephalus (Chiari II obstructs CSF), meningitis, orthopedic deformities, neurogenic bowel/bladder, recurrent UTI, kidney injury
Tethered cord may cause progressive weakness or continence changes during growth
Osteopenic insensate legs: new swelling → **X-ray** for occult fracture

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Folic acid 400–800 µg/day** before conception through early pregnancy for average risk
Prior NTD pregnancy → **4 mg/day**, starting ≥1 month before conception through first 3 months
Optimize diabetes, review antiseizure drugs before pregnancy; avoid prolonged overheating

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sacrococcygeal teratoma: solid/cystic mass, not exposed neural placode
Abdominal wall defect: elevated AFP but bowel outside abdomen on ultrasound

table.title: Lesions
rows: Meninges/CSF herniate; cord remains within canal

neural-tube-defects.evidence: Folate checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/folic-acid/hcp/clinical-overview/), [USPSTF 2023](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/document/ClinicalSummaryFinal/folic-acid-for-the-prevention-of-neural-tube-defects-preventive-medication); remaining content established teaching.

neutropenia.name: Neutropenia
neutropenia.scope: Benign ethnic neutropenia (Duffy-null), drug-induced neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, autoimmune neutropenia, ANC thresholds, evaluation and management
neutropenia.core: Infection risk tracks the depth and duration of neutrophil depletion; fever with severe neutropenia is an antibiotic emergency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cytotoxic chemotherapy, marrow malignancy, viral infection, autoimmune disease, B12/folate/copper deficiency
Clozapine, methimazole, propylthiouracil, TMP–SMX and other drugs can cause agranulocytosis
Duffy-null associated neutrophil counts: stable isolated reduction without increased infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Oral ulcers, gingivitis, recurrent bacterial/fungal infections; inflammatory signs and pus may be absent
Cyclic mouth ulcers/infections suggest cyclic neutropenia; multiple cytopenias suggest marrow disease
Drug-associated fever or sore throat → urgent CBC, especially with antithyroid drugs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced marrow production, peripheral destruction or splenic sequestration lowers circulating neutrophils
Mucosal barrier injury plus impaired innate defense permits rapid invasive bacterial infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ANC = WBC × (% neutrophils + bands)/100**; repeat CBC with differential and smear
Mild: 1000–1500/µL; moderate: 500–1000; **severe <500**; profound <100
★ Febrile neutropenia: **≥38.3°C once or ≥38.0°C for ≥1 hour**, ANC <500 or expected decline
Obtain peripheral/line blood cultures, targeted cultures and imaging without delaying antibiotics
Persistent unexplained severe counts, abnormal smear or other cytopenias → marrow evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Febrile severe neutropenia → **IV cefepime**, piperacillin–tazobactam or meropenem promptly
Add vancomycin for shock, suspected line/skin infection, pneumonia or documented resistant gram-positive infection
★ Stop culprit drug; G-CSF for selected severe/drug-related cases and high-risk chemotherapy settings
Carefully selected low-risk stable patients → oral ciprofloxacin + amoxicillin–clavulanate with reliable close follow-up
High-risk persistent fever 4–7 days → fungal evaluation and empiric **caspofungin**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pseudomonas sepsis, invasive candidiasis/aspergillosis, neutropenic enterocolitis; avoid rectal instrumentation
**Ecthyma gangrenosum**: bulla → painless black necrotic ulcer, Pseudomonas bacteremia; antipseudomonal drug, not steroids

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, oral care; selected prolonged profound neutropenia → antibacterial/antifungal prophylaxis
Stable Duffy-null pattern → reassurance after excluding other causes; no unnecessary G-CSF

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lymphopenia: opportunistic infection risk with preserved ANC
Acute leukemia: blasts and additional cytopenias

obsessive-compulsive-disorder.name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
obsessive-compulsive-disorder.scope: Obsessive-compulsive disorder, ego-dystonic obsessions and compulsions, exposure and response prevention, SSRIs
obsessive-compulsive-disorder.core: Intrusive unwanted thoughts and ritualized acts consume time or impair function; treatment breaks the cycle of anxiety and neutralization.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Often begins in childhood/adolescence; family history, tic disorders, anxiety/depression comorbidity
Stress may worsen symptoms; intrusive harm/sexual thoughts do not alone imply intent

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Ego-dystonic obsessions**: contamination, doubt, symmetry, aggressive or taboo thoughts
Compulsions: washing, checking, counting or mental rituals aimed at preventing feared outcomes
Usually recognizes excessiveness, but insight ranges to absent; reassurance seeking can function as a ritual
Skin injury from washing, lateness or avoidance; severe cases markedly restrict eating or daily activity

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical dysfunction; rituals transiently reduce distress and are negatively reinforced

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical interview**: obsessions/compulsions >1 hour daily or significant distress/impairment
Assess insight, functional effect, suicidality, tics and depression; Yale-Brown scale tracks severity
Exclude substances/medical causes and distinguish repetitive behaviors driven by other disorders

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **CBT with exposure and response prevention**: graded feared-stimulus exposure without ritual completion
★ **SSRI**, e.g., sertraline/fluoxetine; mild-moderate pediatric OCD → ERP alone first; substantial impairment → combine
Often higher tolerated SSRI doses and 8–12-week trial needed; do not label failure after brief exposure
Persistent symptoms → optimize ERP/adherence, switch SSRI or clomipramine; selected resistant disease → risperidone
Reduce family accommodation/reassurance rituals; maintain effective treatment before gradual taper

rows.label: Complications
items: Depression, suicidality, social/occupational disability; dermatitis from compulsive washing
Clomipramine → anticholinergic effects, arrhythmia and overdose risk; SSRI → sexual dysfunction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Generalized anxiety: realistic everyday worries rather than intrusive obsession/neutralization cycle
Psychosis: fixed belief without typical resisted ritual; assess insight carefully

table.title: Related repetitive patterns
rows: Developmental social differences, soothing stereotyped routines
Brief involuntary movement/sound with premonitory urge

obstructive-sleep-apnea.name: Obstructive Sleep Apnea
obstructive-sleep-apnea.scope: risk factors, clinical features (excessive daytime sleepiness, snoring), polysomnography, CPAP, cardiovascular complications
obstructive-sleep-apnea.core: Recurrent upper-airway obstruction during sleep causes intermittent hypoxemia and arousals, often presenting as loud snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, large neck circumference, male sex, aging, retrognathia and upper-airway crowding
Alcohol/sedatives worsen collapse; children often have adenotonsillar hypertrophy; risk rises after menopause

rows.label: Clues
items: Witnessed apneas, gasping/choking, unrefreshing sleep, morning headache, nocturia
Resistant hypertension, atrial fibrillation, secondary polycythemia or recurrent drowsy-driving episodes raise suspicion
Children may show hyperactivity, learning problems, enuresis or poor growth rather than sleepiness
Normal awake oxygen saturation does not exclude severe nocturnal disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sleep-related reduction in pharyngeal tone collapses vulnerable airway despite persistent respiratory effort
Intermittent hypoxia and sympathetic surges drive hypertension; fragmentation impairs attention and vigilance
Sleep-related hypoventilation with nocturnal hypercapnia → morning headaches

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Polysomnography** confirms; screening tools such as STOP-BANG estimate risk, not diagnosis
Uncomplicated high-risk adults → home sleep apnea test acceptable; negative/inconclusive → in-laboratory study
★ AHI **≥5/hour with symptoms/comorbidity**, or ≥15 regardless of symptoms, establishes adult OSA
AHI 5–14 mild, 15–29 moderate, ≥30 severe; pediatric thresholds differ
Cardiorespiratory disease, suspected hypoventilation, chronic opioids or neuromuscular weakness → laboratory polysomnography

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **CPAP** for symptomatic OSA and most moderate/severe disease; optimize mask fit/adherence
Weight loss, exercise, lateral sleep positioning; avoid bedtime alcohol and sedatives
★ CPAP-intolerant or selected mild/moderate disease → **mandibular advancement device**
Child adenotonsillar hypertrophy → adenotonsillectomy, even with pulmonary hypertension; selected adults → surgery, hypoglossal stimulation
Counsel sleepy patients to avoid driving until controlled; do not rely on stimulants before treating obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Systemic hypertension, arrhythmias, stroke risk, pulmonary hypertension in selected patients
Motor vehicle/work accidents, impaired cognition, mood disturbance
Awake postoperative hypercapnia → **CPAP/BiPAP**; reintubate only if obtunded or failing noninvasive support

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain healthy weight, reassess after major weight change; continue PAP around surgery with monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Central apnea: absent respiratory effort during pauses
Narcolepsy: cataplexy and sleep-onset REM features
OHS: persistent daytime hypercapnia

osteoarthritis.name: Osteoarthritis
osteoarthritis.scope: Clinical diagnosis (Heberden/Bouchard nodes, activity-related pain), radiographic findings, nonpharmacologic therapy, oral and topical NSAIDs, injections
osteoarthritis.core: Activity-related joint pain with brief morning stiffness, crepitus and bony enlargement suggests degenerative joint disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, **obesity** (strongest modifiable), prior trauma, malalignment, repetitive occupational loading
Family history, particularly hand disease; obesity affects both mechanical and metabolic risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Morning stiffness generally **<30 minutes**; pain improves with rest early in disease
Knees, hips, first carpometacarpal, DIP and PIP commonly involved; MCP usually spared
Heberden nodes: DIP; Bouchard nodes: PIP; reduced motion and varus/valgus deformity
Hip disease: groin pain with restricted internal rotation; referred pain can localize to knee

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Articular cartilage loss, subchondral remodeling and osteophytes; low-grade synovial inflammation
Joint pain arises from innervated surrounding structures rather than aneural cartilage itself

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical presentation → **clinical diagnosis**; imaging unnecessary for straightforward mild disease
Weight-bearing radiographs if uncertain, severe or worsening: asymmetric joint-space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis/cysts
★ Hot acutely swollen joint → **arthrocentesis**; not an OA flare; mild cool effusion → x-ray, simple analgesic
OA fluid noninflammatory: usually WBC <2000/µL; inflammatory markers generally normal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First-line **exercise, strengthening, weight loss**; cane contralateral to painful hip/knee
★ Knee/hand pain → **topical diclofenac**; oral NSAID if insufficient and renal/GI/CV risks acceptable
Acetaminophen if unable to use NSAIDs (older exam questions may expect it first); duloxetine for persistent pain
Intra-articular glucocorticoid for short-term relief; avoid routine opioids and hyaluronic acid injections
Severe pain/function loss despite conservative treatment → **joint replacement**

rows.label: Complications
items: Functional limitation, falls, reduced activity and secondary deconditioning
NSAIDs → GI bleeding, AKI, fluid retention; arthroplasty → infection or VTE

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Weight loss** best prevents knee OA, beyond exercise alone; conditioning, injury prevention; no complete joint rest

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rheumatoid arthritis: prolonged stiffness, boggy symmetric MCP/wrist synovitis, marginal erosions, DIP spared
CPPD: acute inflammatory flares, chondrocalcinosis
Septic arthritis: fever, severe painful passive motion, positive synovial culture
Trochanteric bursitis: lateral hip pain over greater trochanter, not groin pain

osteoarthritis.evidence: Not checked online; established ACR/Arthritis Foundation principles.

osteomyelitis.name: Osteomyelitis
osteomyelitis.scope: Vertebral osteomyelitis and discitis, hematogenous seeding (S. aureus, IV drug use), contiguous spread (diabetic foot ulcer), probe-to-bone test, MRI, bone biopsy and culture, parenteral antibiotics
osteomyelitis.core: Persistent focal bone or back pain, especially with bacteremia, a deep diabetic ulcer, or elevated inflammatory markers, suggests bone infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hematogenous seeding: S. aureus, endocarditis, injection drug use; vertebral disease often lacks fever
Contiguous spread: diabetic foot ulcers, pressure injury; direct inoculation: open fracture, surgery, hardware
Sickle cell: Salmonella association, but S. aureus remains important; plantar puncture through shoe → Pseudomonas

rows.label: Clues
items: Point tenderness, swelling, drainage or nonhealing sinus; systemic toxicity may be absent
★ New neurologic deficit, saddle anesthesia, urinary retention → **epidural extension/cord compression**
Diabetic ulcer over bony prominence, visible bone, or prolonged failure to heal increases suspicion
Child: fever, point tenderness over long-bone **metaphysis**; septic joint instead limits joint motion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Infected bone develops inflammatory pressure, vascular compromise, and necrosis
Sequestrum: devitalized infected bone; involucrum: reactive new bone; biofilm promotes hardware persistence

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, ESR/CRP, two blood-culture sets; plain films first but early findings can be absent
★ Diabetic foot: **probe-to-bone** plus radiographs/inflammatory markers; MRI if diagnosis remains uncertain
★ **MRI** best for early marrow disease and epidural/paraspinal abscess; bone scan uptake if MRI unavailable
Bone biopsy for histology/culture before antibiotics if stable; superficial wound swabs unreliable
Compatible vertebral MRI plus S. aureus bacteremia usually obviates biopsy; assess endocarditis source

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sepsis or neurologic compromise → cultures then **IV vancomycin + cefepime**, urgent surgical assessment
Stable vertebral disease → obtain microbiologic diagnosis before empiric antibiotics
MSSA → cefazolin/nafcillin; MRSA → vancomycin; tailor to cultures, usually about **6 weeks**
IV initially for serious disease; selected stable patients can complete highly bioavailable oral regimens
Debride necrotic bone/drain abscess; surgery for instability, progressive deficit, or uncontrolled infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Epidural abscess, pathologic fracture, deformity, bacteremia, chronic draining sinus
Longstanding sinus may develop squamous carcinoma; prolonged antibiotics → line infection, renal injury, C. difficile

rows.label: Prevention
items: Diabetic foot inspection, offloading, vascular assessment, glucose control; prompt open-fracture antibiotics and debridement

rows.label: Mimics
items: Charcot arthropathy: neuropathic warm foot, joint fragmentation; MRI/biopsy may distinguish overlapping infection
Bone malignancy: destructive mass, pathology without infection
Degenerative disc disease: mechanical pain without infectious endplate/disc pattern

ovarian-cancer.name: Ovarian cancer
ovarian-cancer.scope: Epithelial ovarian carcinoma, CA-125, pelvic ultrasound, peritoneal carcinomatosis, germ cell tumors, sex cord-stromal tumors, surgical staging and cytoreduction, platinum-based chemotherapy
ovarian-cancer.core: Persistent bloating, early satiety, pelvic symptoms, or an adnexal mass—especially after menopause—requires evaluation for an often late-presenting malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, nulliparity, BRCA1/2 or Lynch syndrome; family history of breast/ovarian cancer
Endometriosis associated with clear-cell/endometrioid subtypes; pregnancy and combined contraceptives reduce epithelial risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Older patient + ascites, large/fixed pelvic mass, weight loss, pleural effusion, obstruction → **epithelial** carcinoma
Young patient with rapidly enlarging mass → germ cell tumor; estrogen/androgen effects → stromal tumor
Postmenopausal bleeding with adnexal mass → consider estrogen-secreting granulosa tumor and endometrial disease
★ **Palpable ovary after menopause** → abnormal (ovaries atrophy); pelvic ultrasound

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Many high-grade serous tumors arise in distal fallopian tube epithelium
Transcoelomic seeding produces peritoneal/omental disease; hormone secretion depends on tumor lineage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** first; solid components, papillary projections, vascularity, ascites increase suspicion
★ **CA-125** supports risk assessment/monitoring, not diagnosis or average-risk screening
Young/complex mass → β-hCG, AFP, LDH; suspected stromal tumor → inhibin/sex hormones
Suspected malignancy → CT abdomen/pelvis/chest and gynecologic oncology; definitive histology and staging usually surgical
Isolated resectable mass → avoid aspiration; advanced disease → biopsy before neoadjuvant chemotherapy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Epithelial carcinoma → **surgical staging/cytoreduction + carboplatin/paclitaxel** according to stage
Poor upfront surgical candidate → tissue confirmation, neoadjuvant platinum chemotherapy, interval cytoreduction
Germ cell malignancy → fertility-sparing surgery when feasible; stage IA dysgerminoma may avoid chemotherapy
Higher-risk germ cell tumors → bleomycin/etoposide/cisplatin
Selected BRCA/HRD-associated disease → PARP-inhibitor maintenance after platinum response

rows.label: Complications
items: Peritoneal carcinomatosis, ascites, malignant obstruction, VTE; chemotherapy neuropathy/myelosuppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **No routine CA-125/ultrasound screening** in asymptomatic average-risk patients
Genetic counseling/testing; hereditary high-risk patients → discuss risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy after childbearing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Endometrioma: cyclic pain, ground-glass ultrasound; CA-125 can rise
Meigs syndrome: benign ovarian fibroma plus ascites/pleural effusion; no peritoneal implants

table.title: Tumor markers
rows: Often bilateral; psammoma bodies; WT1+, p53 abnormal

palliative-and-hospice-care.name: Palliative and hospice care
palliative-and-hospice-care.scope: Hospice eligibility, pain control, goals of care, surrogate requests
palliative-and-hospice-care.core: Palliative care relieves suffering at any illness stage; hospice centers care on comfort when prognosis and patient goals support a terminal-care benefit.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ **Patient goals and informed consent** guide intervention burdens; symptom relief remains an obligation
Proportionate opioids for pain/dyspnea permissible despite risks; reassess sedation/respiration
Codeine fails → morphine/oxycodone; pain mimics depression; wears off early → shorten interval

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Ask understanding/values → discuss prognosis → recommend a goal-concordant plan
Assess capacity; use advance directive, then authorized surrogate: substituted judgment/best interests
★ Titrate **opioids**, short-acting for breakthrough; constipation → keep dose, add stimulant laxative

rows.label: Don't
items: DNR ≠ no antibiotics, fluids, nutrition or other desired treatment
Capable patient’s informed wishes override surrogate requests
No nonbeneficial interventions; explain reasoning, offer alternatives, seek ethics review for conflict

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Refractory terminal suffering → proportional palliative sedation, specialist review and consent
Emergency, unknown preferences → stabilize while clarifying wishes; honor documented refusals
Advanced dementia refusing intake → comfort hand-feeding by mouth; no tubes or IV

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Hospice: **≤6-month prognosis** if usual course; longer survival permits recertification
Hospice: unrelated conditions remain treatable; no DNR requirement; enrollment revocable if goals change
Cancer pain: escalating requests → tolerance/progression, not addiction; past OUD never limits analgesia

palliative-and-hospice-care.evidence: Eligibility checked 2026-10-30: [CMS hospice benefit](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-for-service-providers/hospice); clinical ethics: established teaching.

table.title: Care settings
rows: Adjust with hospice team; avoid readmission

pancreatitis.name: Pancreatitis
pancreatitis.scope: Acute pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis, exocrine and endocrine insufficiency
pancreatitis.core: Epigastric pain radiating to the back with pancreatic inflammation may be acute; repeated injury produces irreversible chronic insufficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gallstones (prior postprandial biliary colic), heavy alcohol, triglycerides >1,000 mg/dL, ERCP, hypercalcemia, medications
Chronic: prolonged alcohol/tobacco exposure, genetic disease, duct obstruction, autoimmune disease
Blunt abdominal trauma + epigastric mass/raised enzymes → contrast CT for pancreatic/duodenal injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Severe constant pain, vomiting, tenderness, ileus; chronic disease adds steatorrhea and weight loss
★ **Hypoxemia, hypotension, oliguria, persistent SIRS** → early monitored/ICU assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature intrapancreatic enzyme activation → autodigestion and systemic inflammation
Chronic fibrosis destroys acinar/islet tissue: ↓insulin, ↓glucagon, normal insulin sensitivity; lipase may normalize

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute diagnosis: **2 of 3**—typical pain, lipase or amylase ≥3× ULN, characteristic imaging
RUQ ultrasound evaluates gallstones; triglycerides, calcium, liver tests identify cause
Contrast CT: diagnostic doubt, high fever/marked leukocytosis (necrosis?), deterioration, no improvement by 48–72 hours; not routine early
Chronic: CT/MRCP shows calcification/duct changes; fecal elastase <200 supports exocrine insufficiency
Recurrent, no gallstones/alcohol → EUS or MRCP for ductal anatomy; older exam questions may expect ERCP

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute: **moderate lactated Ringer resuscitation**, reassessment, IV opioid analgesia, electrolyte correction; avoid overload
★ **Early oral low-fat feeding** by 48 hours if tolerated; else enteral; older exam questions may expect initial bowel rest
Biliary with cholangitis → urgent ERCP; mild gallstone disease → cholecystectomy before discharge
Uncomplicated/sterile: no antibiotics; infected necrosis: penetrating antibiotics, delayed step-up drainage/debridement
Chronic: stop alcohol/tobacco; pancrelipase, fat-soluble vitamins, pain control; islet-loss diabetes → **insulin**, not sulfonylureas

rows.label: Complications
items: ARDS, AKI, shock, hypocalcemia; necrosis, hemorrhage; **splenic vein thrombosis** → isolated gastric varices, normal liver
Pseudocyst after >4 weeks; infected collection, obstruction; chronic disease → pancreatic cancer and brittle diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Treat cause**: gallbladder removal, triglyceride control, avoid culprit drug and alcohol
Post-ERCP rectal indomethacin in eligible patients; selected pancreatic duct stenting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Perforated ulcer: rigid abdomen/free air
Mesenteric ischemia: pain-exam mismatch; MI: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern

table.title: Severity and collections
rows: Transient dysfunction ≤48 hours or local complication

panic-disorder.name: Panic disorder
panic-disorder.scope: Panic attack criteria, unexpected recurrent attacks, agoraphobia, acute abortive therapy, maintenance therapy, medical rule-outs
panic-disorder.core: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks followed by at least 1 month of fear of recurrence or maladaptive behavioral change establish panic disorder.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young adulthood, family history, trauma, anxiety sensitivity
Caffeine, stimulants, cannabis, decongestants, hyperthyroidism, withdrawal can provoke paniclike symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Abrupt intense fear peaks within minutes; palpitations, dyspnea, chest pain, paresthesias, derealization
Attack requires ≥4 characteristic symptoms; fear of dying/losing control common
★ **Syncope, exertional onset, hypoxemia, focal findings**, sustained arrhythmia → medical cause until evaluated
Agoraphobia: fear/avoidance of ≥2 situations where escape/help seems difficult, persisting ≥6 months

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Threat-circuit overactivation and catastrophic interpretation of benign sensations amplify autonomic symptoms
Hyperventilation lowers CO₂ → lightheadedness, perioral/distal tingling; avoidance reinforces anticipatory fear
**Sodium lactate infusion** provokes attacks: heightened panic sensitivity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis after medical/substance review**; unexpected episodes distinguish disorder from predictable triggers
Vital signs, examination, ECG for cardiopulmonary symptoms; glucose/TSH or toxicology guided by history
Chest pain risk → ACS/PE evaluation rather than automatic psychiatric attribution
Assess depression, suicidality, substance use; agoraphobia may be diagnosed separately

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ During attack → **calm reassurance, slow breathing**, reduce stimulation after excluding danger
Severe acute episode → short-term lorazepam when needed; avoid with sedatives or substance-use risk
★ Maintenance → **CBT with interoceptive exposure and/or SSRI**, such as sertraline
Start SSRI low, titrate slowly; benefit takes weeks; venlafaxine alternative
Continue effective treatment after remission, then gradual taper; benzodiazepines not preferred long-term

rows.label: Complications
items: Agoraphobic avoidance, impaired function, depression, self-medication with alcohol
Benzodiazepine dependence/withdrawal; alprazolam → **between-dose rebound anxiety**; SSRIs may initially increase anxiety

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Reduce caffeine/stimulants**, regular sleep/exercise, practice exposure and relapse-prevention skills
Paper-bag rebreathing discouraged (hypoxemia risk); older exam questions may expect it if SpO₂ normal

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: persistent tremor, heat intolerance, low TSH
SVT: documented abrupt regular tachycardia, not solely subjective palpitations
Social anxiety: fear tied to scrutiny rather than unexpected attacks
Mitral valve prolapse: incidental click/murmur; doesn't explain recurrent attacks with fear of recurrence

panic-disorder.evidence: Not checked online; established DSM-5-TR and anxiety treatment teaching.

parasitic-infections.name: Parasitic infections
parasitic-infections.scope: Strongyloidiasis, giardiasis, amebiasis, cryptosporidiosis, ascariasis, schistosomiasis, pinworm (enterobiasis), cysticercosis, eosinophilia workup, antiparasitic therapy
parasitic-infections.core: Exposure, organ pattern, and immune status identify the parasite; eosinophilia favors tissue-invasive helminths rather than intestinal protozoa.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Contaminated food/water, endemic travel, freshwater contact, barefoot soil exposure, household crowding
Steroids/HTLV-1 predispose to Strongyloides hyperinfection; advanced HIV predisposes to persistent cryptosporidiosis

rows.label: Clues
items: Ascariasis: transient cough/eosinophilic infiltrates during larval migration; later intestinal or biliary obstruction
Pinworm: nocturnal perianal/vulvar itch, dysuria with normal UA; household clustering
Cysticercosis: seizures or hydrocephalus; ingestion of **T. solium eggs**, not pork cysts
Cutaneous larva migrans: soil contact; pruritic **serpiginous tracks**; animal hookworm larvae → albendazole or ivermectin

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Giardia blunts microvilli → **fat/carbohydrate malabsorption**; invasive protozoa can affect liver, urinary tract, or CNS
Strongyloides autoinfection permits lifelong persistence and dissemination after immunosuppression

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Unexplained **eosinophilia** → travel/drug history, serial stool O&P, targeted Strongyloides serology
★ Steroids + eosinophilia or infiltrates → **Strongyloides hyperinfection**: **duodenal aspirate** larvae; stool O&P often misses
Diarrhea → stool antigen/PCR for protozoa; single routine O&P can miss infection
★ Pinworm → **morning tape test** before washing; stool testing insensitive
Brain MRI/CT for cysticercosis; eye examination before antiparasitics; assess lesion viability and location

rows.label: Tx
items: Rehydrate; ascariasis → albendazole; bowel obstruction → surgical evaluation before deworming
Pinworm → albendazole, mebendazole, or pyrantel; repeat after **2 weeks**, treat household simultaneously
★ Viable parenchymal cysticercosis → albendazole ± praziquantel with corticosteroids; seizures → levetiracetam
Calcified brain lesions → no antiparasitic; hydrocephalus → neurosurgical control before cysticidal treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Strongyloides hyperinfection → gram-negative sepsis, respiratory failure; eosinophilia may disappear
Amebic liver abscess; schistosomiasis → portal hypertension or bladder squamous carcinoma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Screen/treat Strongyloides before **immunosuppression** after endemic exposure
Safe water, sanitation, handwashing, footwear; avoid endemic freshwater and untreated swimming water
Neurocysticercosis household contacts → **stool O&P** to find egg-shedding T. solium tapeworm carrier

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBD: chronic inflammatory diarrhea after infection excluded
Drug hypersensitivity: eosinophilia linked to new medication, rash or organ injury

table.title: Exposure → diagnosis and treatment
rows: Camping; greasy stool, bloating; stool antigen
Dysentery, flask-shaped ulcers; stool PCR; abscess → serology
Soil; larva currens, larvae in stool
Ivermectin; hyperinfection requires prolonged daily treatment
Freshwater; hematuria (haematobium), portal fibrosis (mansoni/japonicum); eggs, serology
Confirmed E. histolytica without invasive disease

pediatric-neck-masses.name: Pediatric neck masses
pediatric-neck-masses.scope: Thyroglossal duct cyst, branchial cleft cyst, cystic hygroma (lymphatic malformation), congenital muscular torticollis (fibromatosis colli), cervical lymphadenitis
pediatric-neck-masses.core: Childhood neck lump: location, mobility with swallowing, tenderness, and head posture separate congenital remnants from inflammatory lymph nodes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Congenital anomalies may enlarge during URI; lymphatic malformation associated with Turner syndrome
Bacterial lymphadenitis: Staphylococcus aureus, group A Streptococcus; dental disease → oral anaerobes
Fibromatosis colli: infancy, intrauterine positioning or birth-related sternocleidomastoid injury

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Stridor, drooling, respiratory distress** → threatened airway; immediate stabilization
★ Hard, fixed, supraclavicular, enlarging mass or weight loss/night sweats → **malignancy evaluation**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryologic tract persistence, abnormal lymphatic channels, muscle fibrosis, or reactive/infected lymphoid tissue

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Neck ultrasound first** for superficial mass; distinguish cystic/solid lesions and detect abscess
Before midline cyst excision → confirm normally located thyroid; ectopic thyroid may be sole functioning tissue
Deep infection/airway compression → contrast CT; extensive lymphatic lesion → MRI
Persistent unexplained concerning node → excisional biopsy; CBC/differential guides hematologic evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat infection before elective congenital cyst surgery**
Toxic child, oral intolerance, or treatment failure → IV cefazolin; MRSA concern → vancomycin
Fluctuant bacterial abscess → drainage plus culture; dental source → amoxicillin-clavulanate

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent infection, abscess, airway compression; untreated torticollis → plagiocephaly and facial asymmetry

rows.label: Prevention
items: Complete tract removal reduces cyst recurrence; early positioning exercises prevent secondary deformity
Oral hygiene and dental treatment reduce odontogenic lymphadenitis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reactive nodes: bilateral, mobile, recent URI; usually regress with observation
Atypical mycobacteria: chronic unilateral node, violaceous skin; excision rather than routine abscess incision
Lymphoma: rubbery, persistent nodes with systemic symptoms

table.title: Location → diagnosis → treatment
rows: SCM lump; ipsilateral tilt, opposite chin

pediatric-neck-masses.evidence: Checked 2026-11-05: [CHOP neck masses](https://www.chop.edu/conditions-diseases/neck-masses); established pediatric diagnostic approach.

pericardial-disease.name: Pericardial disease
pericardial-disease.scope: Acute pericarditis, pericardial effusion, tamponade, constrictive pericarditis
pericardial-disease.core: Pericardial inflammation, fluid accumulation, or fibrosis produces distinct chest-pain and impaired-filling syndromes; hemodynamic effect depends on accumulation rate.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Viral/idiopathic, autoimmune disease, uremia, malignancy, TB, radiation, cardiac surgery
Early post-MI inflammation or delayed immune-mediated Dressler syndrome; trauma/anticoagulation can cause hemopericardium

rows.label: Clues
items: Pericarditis: sharp pleuritic positional pain, better leaning forward; friction rub may be transient
★ Tamponade: **hypotension, elevated JVP, muffled sounds**, pulsus paradoxus >10 mmHg; triad often incomplete
Constrictive disease: edema/ascites, Kussmaul sign, pericardial knock, prominent y descent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflamed surfaces cause pain; fluid or scar limits diastolic filling and stroke volume
Tamponade equalizes diastolic pressures; constriction exaggerates ventricular interdependence with respiration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pericarditis: ≥2 of **typical pain, rub, diffuse ST elevation/PR depression, new effusion**
Troponin elevation suggests myocardial involvement; CRP supports inflammation; echo assesses fluid and ventricular function
★ **Urgent bedside echo** for suspected tamponade: right-sided chamber collapse, plethoric IVC
Constrictive suspicion → echo, CT/MRI for thickening/calcification; catheterization if diagnosis remains uncertain

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tamponade → **urgent pericardiocentesis**; IV fluids bridge; avoid diuresis/positive-pressure ventilation
Purulent, traumatic, malignant, or recurrent effusion → surgical drainage/window; antibiotics for bacterial cause
Stable effusion → treat cause, serial echo; low voltage alone never determines drainage
High-risk features → admit: fever, large effusion, immunosuppression, anticoagulation, subacute onset, NSAID failure
Early post-cardiac-surgery tamponade → **urgent mediastinal re-exploration**

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent inflammation, arrhythmia/myocarditis, obstructive shock; procedural drainage → cardiac injury
Rapid decompression can rarely cause ventricular dysfunction; NSAIDs → GI/renal injury, colchicine → diarrhea

rows.label: Prevention
items: Colchicine course: first episode 3 months; recurrence ≥6 months; taper anti-inflammatory drugs after remission
Exercise restriction until clinical/inflammatory resolution; optimize dialysis for uremic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: STEMI: regional ST elevation with reciprocal changes; urgent coronary evaluation if uncertain
Restrictive cardiomyopathy: myocardial disease, less respiratory ventricular discordance
PE: thrombotic risk, acute RV strain

table.title: Nonemergency definitive management
rows: Ibuprofen + colchicine; aspirin preferred after MI
Selected low-dose glucocorticoid or IL-1 blockade

peripheral-neuropathy.name: Peripheral neuropathy
peripheral-neuropathy.scope: Distal symmetric polyneuropathy, chemotherapy-induced (cisplatin, paclitaxel), HIV-associated neuropathy, alcohol-related, neuropathic pain pharmacotherapy (TCAs, gabapentinoids, SNRIs)
peripheral-neuropathy.core: Length-dependent injury produces symmetric distal sensory symptoms beginning in the feet and progressing proximally before the hands become involved.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Diabetes, alcohol use, CKD, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, HIV
Cisplatin/paclitaxel exposure; older neurotoxic ART such as stavudine; malnutrition

rows.label: Clues
items: Burning pain, allodynia or numbness; reduced vibration, ankle reflexes and distal sensation
★ **Asymmetry, rapid progression, motor predominance or marked autonomic findings** → urgent expanded evaluation
Small-fiber neuropathy: pain/temperature loss with initially preserved strength and nerve conduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Axonal dying-back affects longest fibers first; demyelinating neuropathy produces disproportionate conduction slowing

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Glucose/A1c, B12 with methylmalonic acid if borderline, SPEP with immunofixation**
CBC, metabolic panel, TSH; HIV testing according to exposure and clinical context
EMG/nerve conduction for atypical features, unclear diagnosis, or suspected demyelination
Normal studies do not exclude small-fiber disease; skin biopsy can confirm selected cases

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat cause: glycemic control, B12, alcohol cessation/nutrition, optimize ART; review neurotoxic drugs
★ Pain → **duloxetine, gabapentin/pregabalin, or TCA**; choose by comorbidity and adverse effects
Gabapentinoids: sedation/edema, renal dose adjustment; TCAs: anticholinergic effects, cardiac risk in older adults
★ Painful chemotherapy neuropathy → **duloxetine**; discuss dose reduction/substitution with oncology
Topical lidocaine/capsaicin for localized symptoms; avoid chronic opioids

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, painless ulcers, infection, Charcot arthropathy; orthostatic hypotension with autonomic involvement
Pain treatment reduces symptoms without restoring lost sensation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Daily foot inspection, protective footwear, monofilament assessment, fall prevention
Treat nutritional deficiencies; monitor symptoms during neurotoxic chemotherapy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Radiculopathy: dermatomal, often asymmetric pain and weakness
Myelopathy: hyperreflexia, sensory level, bowel/bladder dysfunction
Peripheral arterial disease: exertional pain, reduced pulses rather than sensory stocking loss
Charcot-Marie-Tooth: adolescent **pes cavus, hammer toes**, distal wasting, slowed conduction, family history

pharyngitis.name: Pharyngitis
pharyngitis.scope: Centor score, Group A Streptococcus, rapid antigen detection, throat culture, viral pharyngitis, penicillin, peritonsillar abscess
pharyngitis.core: Most sore throats are viral; identify patients needing group A streptococcal testing and recognize deep-space infection or airway danger.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: School-age children, close contacts, crowded settings, winter/spring; GAS uncommon below age 3
Smoking, immunosuppression, incomplete vaccination broaden infectious differential

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Cough, rhinorrhea, conjunctivitis, oral ulcers** favor viral cause; avoid unnecessary GAS testing
Centor: fever, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical nodes, absence of cough; 1 point each
McIsaac modifies by age; score 0–1 → no test, no antibiotic; scoring never proves bacterial infection
★ **Trismus, muffled voice, unilateral bulge, uvular deviation** → peritonsillar abscess

rows.label: Pathophys
items: GAS pharyngeal infection can trigger immune-mediated rheumatic fever or glomerulonephritis
Tonsillitis → peritonsillar pus: **GAS** commonest, often mixed anaerobes; deeper spread threatens airway, vessels

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ No clear viral syndrome and elevated clinical score → **rapid antigen test or NAAT**
Negative rapid antigen in symptomatic child ≥3 → throat culture; adults usually need no backup
Positive test with compatible illness → treat; asymptomatic carriage generally needs no eradication
Abscess usually clinical; ultrasound/contrast neck CT if uncertain or deep-space extension suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Confirmed GAS → **penicillin or amoxicillin for 10 days**; IM benzathine penicillin if adherence uncertain
Penicillin allergy: cephalexin if nonimmediate; azithromycin/clindamycin if immediate, accounting for local resistance
Viral illness → fluids, warm saline gargle, acetaminophen/ibuprofen; no antibiotics
★ Peritonsillar abscess → **drainage + amoxicillin-clavulanate**; airway assessment, IV ampicillin-sulbactam if severe

rows.label: Complications
items: Rheumatic fever prevented by timely GAS antibiotics; poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis not reliably prevented
Retropharyngeal spread, airway obstruction; Fusobacterium → internal jugular thrombophlebitis/Lemierre syndrome

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene; remain home until afebrile and ≥12–24 hours after effective GAS antibiotics
Do not routinely test asymptomatic household contacts or obtain test-of-cure

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV: posterior nodes, splenomegaly, amoxicillin-associated rash
Epiglottitis: drooling, tripod posture, stridor; avoid provocative throat examination
Diphtheria: adherent gray membrane, incomplete vaccination

physician-patient-communication.name: Physician-patient communication
physician-patient-communication.scope: Medical interpreters, limited English proficiency, delivering bad news, empathetic communication, family requests to withhold information
physician-patient-communication.core: Respect autonomy through understandable, honest, empathic dialogue; identify what patients understand and want before sharing decisions or sensitive information.

rows.label: Principle
items: Confidentiality, cultural humility, informed choice; language barriers never imply impaired capacity
Patient preferences determine family involvement and desired level of disclosure
**Comprehensive, contextual care**: whole-person, longitudinal; tailored to culture, family, goals

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Qualified medical interpreter**, free to patient; speak directly to patient in short segments
★ Bad news: privacy → understanding/preferences → warning → plain disclosure → empathy → plan
Validate emotion; open questions, silence, teach-back; explore beliefs before correcting misinformation

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid jargon, false reassurance, interrupting, arguing, blaming, or premature advice
Avoid routine reliance on children/family for interpreting consent or sensitive discussions
Avoid promising cure or confidentiality beyond legal limits

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ **Family requests nondisclosure → ask patient privately**; patient preferences control disclosure
Capable patient may decline details or designate another recipient; document preference
Emergency without interpreter → temporary available help while securing qualified interpretation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Therapeutic privilege is narrow**; anticipated distress alone never justifies withholding diagnosis
Anger → acknowledge concern, clarify cause, establish boundaries if threatening; no reflex discharge
Requested adult-family interpreter → verify suitability/privacy/voluntariness; offer professional

table.title: Difficult conversations
rows: Pause; allow feelings; schedule prompt follow-up
Voice openly in patient's presence; no covert action
Capable patient hides news from family
Encourage support; respect privacy; never lie to family
Child asks prognosis, parents forbid disclosure
Explore understanding; encourage talking with parents; never lie
Negotiate adherence contract; punitive control backfires
Fluent bilingual staff acceptable; never a child

physician-patient-communication.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [HHS interpreter guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/civil-rights/for-individuals/faqs/may-an-lep-person-use-a-family-member-as-an-interpreter/index.html); established autonomy and bad-news communication principles.

physiologic-changes-of-aging.name: Physiologic changes of aging
physiologic-changes-of-aging.scope: Neurologic changes, sensory changes (presbyopia, presbycusis), sleep architecture changes (early wake, reduced total sleep), cardiovascular stiffening, renal decline, pulmonary compliance
physiologic-changes-of-aging.core: Normal aging reduces organ reserve; preserved everyday independence distinguishes expected slowing from disease.

rows.label: Definition
items: Gradual changes across systems; marked disability requires evaluation rather than attribution to age
Presbyopia: reduced accommodation; presbycusis: bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ Slower processing and recall; **orientation and learned knowledge preserved**
★ Less slow-wave, more awakenings, earlier timing, less total sleep → **reassure**, no hypnotics
★ Isolated **↓ankle reflexes**, ↓toe vibration, impaired tandem, full strength → normal; no workup

rows.label: Use when
items: Reduced baroreflexes and maximal heart rate → orthostatic susceptibility, reduced exercise capacity
Lower renal clearance → adjust renally eliminated drugs despite normal-looking creatinine
Decreased vital capacity and cough reserve → greater respiratory illness vulnerability

rows.label: Compare
items: ★ **Arterial stiffness** → widened pulse pressure; ventricular relaxation slows
Reduced lung elastic recoil → increased lung compliance; chest wall compliance decreases
Declining concentration/dilution → fluid imbalance; reduced muscle mass lowers creatinine production

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Delirium, dementia, falls, incontinence** require evaluation; never inevitable normal aging
Depression or sedatives can explain daytime sleepiness; severe insomnia needs investigation
Unilateral hearing loss, focal weakness, **rotatory nystagmus**, rapid memory loss → disease workup

physiologic-changes-of-aging.evidence: Not checked online; established geriatric physiology.

pituitary-adenomas.name: Pituitary adenomas
pituitary-adenomas.scope: Prolactinoma, acromegaly, nonfunctioning adenoma, pituitary apoplexy
pituitary-adenomas.core: Pituitary tumors cause hormone excess, pituitary failure, or sellar mass effects; determine functional status before choosing medical treatment or surgery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Most sporadic; MEN1 with associated parathyroid/pancreatic endocrine tumors
Apoplexy may follow tumor hemorrhage/infarction, anticoagulation, pregnancy or major physiologic stress

rows.label: Clues
items: Mass effect → headache and bitemporal hemianopia from optic-chiasm compression
Pituitary failure → fatigue, hypotension, low libido; prolactin-related gonadal suppression may cause infertility
★ **Sudden severe headache, visual loss, ophthalmoplegia, hypotension** → pituitary apoplexy
GH excess may cause macroglossia, prognathism, enlarged hands/feet and worsening ring/shoe size

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Autonomous secretion causes hormone excess; stalk compression interrupts dopamine inhibition, modestly raising prolactin
Expanding sellar tissue compresses normal pituitary and optic pathways; acute infarction can eliminate ACTH reserve

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Hormonal assessment → **contrast pituitary MRI**; formal visual fields if lesion abuts chiasm
Check prolactin, IGF-1, AM cortisol, free T4/TSH and gonadal axis; screen cortisol excess when clinically suspected
Elevated prolactin → exclude pregnancy, hypothyroidism, renal failure and dopamine-blocking drugs
Large mass with unexpectedly modest prolactin → dilute assay for **hook effect**
Acromegaly: elevated age-adjusted IGF-1 → failure of GH suppression after oral glucose

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected apoplexy → **IV hydrocortisone immediately**, fluids, urgent MRI and neurosurgical/endocrine assessment
Persistent severe visual deficits or reduced consciousness → urgent decompression after stabilization
★ Replace glucocorticoids **before levothyroxine** when both axes deficient
Prolactinoma → **cabergoline**, even with visual deficits; older exam questions may expect bromocriptine
Residual GH excess after surgery → octreotide/lanreotide or pegvisomant; radiation for selected refractory tumors

rows.label: Complications
items: Visual loss, adrenal crisis, hypogonadism; surgery → CSF leak, diabetes insipidus or panhypopituitarism
Acromegaly → cardiomyopathy, diabetes, sleep apnea, colon neoplasia; cabergoline → nausea/orthostasis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Craniopharyngioma: suprasellar cystic/calcified lesion, often childhood onset
Primary hypothyroidism: ↑TSH/↓free T4 with secondary prolactin elevation; medication effect: no autonomous tumor secretion

pituitary-adenomas.evidence: Prolactinoma checked 2026-10-30: [Pituitary Society consensus, 2023](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41574-023-00886-5); other sellar emergencies: established teaching.

table.title: Subtype-directed management
rows: Observe if small; surgery for compression

pleural-effusion.name: Pleural effusion
pleural-effusion.scope: Transudate vs exudate (Light criteria), parapneumonic effusion, empyema, malignant effusion
pleural-effusion.core: Fluid in the pleural space causes dyspnea, dullness, and reduced breath sounds; classify by mechanism and identify infection requiring drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome; pneumonia, malignancy, pulmonary embolism, TB
Recent thoracic surgery, pancreatitis, esophageal rupture, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Pleuritic pain, reduced fremitus; large effusion shifts mediastinum away; unilateral + cancer history → malignant
Fever or persistent sepsis despite antibiotics suggests complicated parapneumonic fluid/empyema
Bloody fluid: malignancy (prior cancer, mediastinal mass), embolism, trauma; milky → chyle
Foul-smelling pus after aspiration → **anaerobic empyema**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transudate: altered hydrostatic/oncotic pressure; exudate: increased permeability or impaired lymphatic drainage
Heart-failure transudate: pleural protein <3 g/dL, low LDH and cell count; **glucose equals serum**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Chest radiograph → **ultrasound-guided thoracentesis** for new unexplained, unilateral, or atypical effusion
Classic bilateral heart-failure effusions → diuresis first; sample if fever, asymmetry, or treatment failure
★ **Exudate if any Light criterion** positive; compare paired pleural and serum measurements
Pleural pH, glucose, cell differential, Gram stain/culture; cytology if cancer suspected
Diuresis can create pseudoexudate; serum–pleural albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL supports transudate

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat systemic cause; therapeutic thoracentesis for significant symptoms; avoid rapid excessive drainage
★ Pus, positive Gram stain/culture, **pH <7.20** or glucose <60 → empyema/complicated: chest tube, antibiotics
Loculated infected fluid → intrapleural tPA/DNase; persistent sepsis → VATS evaluation
★ Recurrent symptomatic malignancy → **indwelling pleural catheter** or pleurodesis; trapped lung favors catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, loculation, trapped lung, respiratory compromise
Thoracentesis → pneumothorax, bleeding, reexpansion pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Heart-failure control, prompt pneumonia treatment; ultrasound guidance reduces procedural injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atelectasis: mediastinal shift toward volume loss
Consolidation: increased fremitus, bronchial breath sounds
Pneumothorax: hyperresonance rather than dullness

pleural-effusion.evidence: Not checked online; established pleural disease teaching.

postpartum-care.name: Postpartum care
postpartum-care.scope: Normal puerperal changes, lochia, uterine involution, perineal and cesarean wound healing, breastfeeding, postpartum depression screening, routine postpartum visit
postpartum-care.core: Postpartum care is an ongoing assessment of recovery, mood, infant feeding, contraception, and chronic disease after every birth.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All postpartum patients; assess support, sleep, safety, sexual health, and reproductive goals

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Contact within **3 weeks**; comprehensive visit by **12 weeks**, with earlier risk-based review
Hypertensive disorder → BP within 7–10 days; severe hypertension → within 72 hours

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Edinburgh or PHQ-9 depression screen; assess suicidality directly after positive self-harm response
BP, bleeding, fundal tenderness; inspect perineum/incision for erythema, drainage, separation
Observe latch/milk transfer; frequent feeds, lactation support; cracked nipples → correct positioning

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Heavy bleeding (pad soaked <1 hour), fever, dyspnea, severe headache → urgent evaluation
Mood screen positive → diagnostic interview, psychotherapy/SSRI; psychosis → emergency hospitalization
Increasing wound pain/purulence → evaluate infection; breast fluctuance → ultrasound for abscess

rows.label: Traps
items: Ovulation may precede first period; discuss contraception before discharge
Lactational contraception: amenorrhea, exclusive frequent breastfeeding, infant <6 months
Postpartum hypertension and cardiomyopathy can first appear after discharge

table.title: Expected recovery
rows: Red rubra → pink serosa → white/yellow alba
Descends daily; near prepregnancy size by 6 weeks
Pain improves; pulling normal if intact; keep clean
Early cramping and fluid loss; breastfeeding intensifies cramping

postpartum-care.evidence: Visit timing checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG postpartum care](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/05/optimizing-postpartum-care); normal physiology established teaching.

postpartum-hemorrhage.name: Postpartum hemorrhage
postpartum-hemorrhage.scope: Primary postpartum hemorrhage (uterine atony, lacerations, retained placenta, coagulopathy), secondary postpartum hemorrhage (retained products of conception, endometritis), barrier methods, surgical management
postpartum-hemorrhage.core: Excessive bleeding after delivery demands simultaneous resuscitation and cause-directed control: Tone, Trauma, Tissue and Thrombin.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Uterine overdistention, prolonged/augmented labor, chorioamnionitis, magnesium, prior PPH → atony
Operative delivery → trauma; placenta accreta/retention → tissue; abruption/sepsis → coagulopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Boggy enlarged uterus** → atony; firm uterus with bleeding → laceration or other cause
Jagged/incomplete placenta, vessels to membrane edge (**succenturiate lobe**) → retained tissue; oozing → coagulopathy
Shock exceeding visible loss → concealed hematoma; post-cesarean distention, hematocrit drop → **intra-abdominal hemorrhage**
Delayed bleeding >24 hours to weeks postpartum → retained products, endometritis or subinvolution

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myometrial contraction compresses placental-bed vessels; failed contraction or disrupted tissue prevents hemostasis
Vulvar hematoma: **pudendal artery** branch, often operative delivery; vaginal/uterine arteries → deep or retroperitoneal

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantify blood loss; US definition **≥1000 mL or hypovolemia within 24 hours**, regardless of route
WHO 2025 earlier treatment trigger: ≥500 mL, or ≥300 mL with abnormal hemodynamic signs
Assess uterine tone, inspect birth canal/placenta; CBC, coagulation studies, fibrinogen and crossmatch
Ultrasound for suspected retained products; avoid delaying control in active unstable bleeding
Inversion: round fleshy introitus mass after cord traction, absent abdominal fundus, shock

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hemorrhage team, two large IVs, warmed balanced blood resuscitation; massage, empty bladder, **oxytocin**
★ **Tranexamic acid within 3 hours** alongside first-response treatment
Refractory atony → **balloon/vacuum**, embolization if stable; compression sutures/arterial ligation or hysterectomy
Laceration → repair; retained tissue → evacuation; inversion → manual replacement before uterotonics
Endometritis → **clindamycin + gentamicin**

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, AKI, shock, death; severe ischemia → Sheehan syndrome
Transfusion complications and hysterectomy-related fertility loss; delayed anemia impairs recovery

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prophylactic **oxytocin after delivery**, active third-stage management and antenatal anemia treatment
Risk assessment, blood availability and team readiness; routine prophylactic TXA not recommended for vaginal birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Amniotic fluid embolism: sudden hypoxia/collapse with DIC
Pulmonary embolism: hypoxia/chest pain without primary uterine blood loss

potassium-disorders.name: Potassium disorders
potassium-disorders.scope: Hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, cardiac membrane stabilization, shift therapy, elimination
potassium-disorders.core: Potassium abnormalities can cause weakness and fatal arrhythmias; stabilize cardiac risk while identifying the cause and correcting total-body balance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hyperkalemia: AKI/CKD, RAAS blockers, potassium-sparing diuretics, tissue lysis, insulin deficiency
Hypokalemia: GI losses, loop/thiazide diuretics, hyperaldosteronism, insulin/beta-agonists, magnesium depletion

rows.label: Clues
items: Flaccid weakness, paralysis, palpitations; symptoms may be absent despite dangerous levels
★ **K ≥6.5 mmol/L, ECG changes, or rapid rise** → emergency; normal ECG not reassuring
Bradycardia/high-degree AV block with renal failure → suspect hyperkalemia; calcium before pacemaker

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Extracellular K changes alter membrane excitability and cardiac conduction
Acidosis/insulin deficiency shift K outward; intracellular shifts can coexist with severe total-body depletion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG + repeat potassium**, creatinine, glucose, bicarbonate, magnesium; assess drugs and acid-base status
Hemolysis, thrombocytosis/leukocytosis → pseudohyperkalemia; repeat atraumatic draw if clinically compatible
Hypokalemia: urine K distinguishes renal wasting from extrarenal loss; interpret with BP/acid-base pattern
Do not delay treatment for confirmatory blood draw when malignant ECG changes present

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hyperkalemic ECG changes or dialysis-patient arrest → **IV calcium gluconate/chloride first**; protects myocardium only
★ Shift K inward: **IV insulin + dextrose**, nebulized albuterol; bicarbonate mainly with significant acidosis
Remove K: loop diuretic if urine output, selected binders; urgent dialysis for severe refractory/renal-failure cases
Mild/stable hypokalemia → oral KCl; <2.5, arrhythmia, paralysis, or no oral access → monitored IV replacement
★ **Correct magnesium deficiency** for refractory low K; never give IV potassium push; monitor glucose after insulin

rows.label: Complications
items: Ventricular arrhythmia, cardiac arrest, respiratory muscle failure
Overcorrection, rebound dyskalemia; insulin-induced hypoglycemia; IV potassium extravasation/phlebitis
Diuretic hypokalemia → **digoxin toxicity**, multifocal PVCs; check K first

rows.label: Prevention
items: Review supplements/salt substitutes; monitor K/creatinine after diuretic or RAAS-drug changes
Treat diarrhea/vomiting and underlying mineralocorticoid disorders; replace ongoing losses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Guillain-Barré: ascending areflexic weakness without explanatory electrolyte pattern
Periodic paralysis: episodic shifts, sometimes thyrotoxicosis; avoid excessive replacement causing rebound

table.title: ECG patterns
rows: Peaked T → PR prolongation → wide QRS/sine-wave
Flat T, ST depression, prominent U waves

potassium-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established electrolyte emergency principles.

prelabor-rupture-of-membranes.name: Prelabor rupture of membranes
prelabor-rupture-of-membranes.scope: Term PROM (induction vs expectant), PPROM (<34 weeks), latency antibiotics, antenatal corticosteroids, magnesium sulfate neuroprotection, complications (chorioamnionitis, placental abruption, pulmonary hypoplasia)
prelabor-rupture-of-membranes.core: Membrane rupture before labor: term PROM favors induction; stable early PPROM favors monitored pregnancy prolongation with infection prevention and fetal maturation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previous PPROM/preterm birth, genital infection, smoking, short cervix, uterine overdistension

rows.label: Clues
items: Sudden gush or persistent watery leakage; reduced fluid volume may develop
★ Fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia → **intra-amniotic infection**; pain/bleeding → possible abruption

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Membrane weakening permits fluid loss and ascending infection; latency inversely related to gestational age

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sterile speculum examination**: pooling or fluid leaking from cervical os
Nitrazine alkaline pH and ferning support diagnosis; blood, semen, vaginitis cause false-positive pH
Equivocal → amniotic protein assay; ultrasound supports, never independently confirms rupture
★ Avoid **digital cervical examinations** unless delivery imminent; assess fetal status and presentation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Infection, fetal compromise, significant abruption, or prolapsed cord → **deliver regardless of gestational age**
Expectant <34 weeks → 7-day latency antibiotics: IV ampicillin/erythromycin then oral amoxicillin/erythromycin
Azithromycin may replace erythromycin; avoid amoxicillin-clavulanate because neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis risk
Preterm birth expected → complete **betamethasone ×2, 24 hours apart**; magnesium sulfate if birth <32 weeks
GBS-positive/unknown-risk labor → penicillin; avoid late-preterm latency antibiotics and prolonged tocolysis

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal/neonatal infection, prematurity, placental abruption, cord compression/prolapse
Early prolonged rupture → pulmonary hypoplasia and limb contractures

rows.label: Prevention
items: Stop smoking, treat identified infections, manage short cervix/prior preterm birth risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Urinary leakage: urine odor, no pooling/ferning
Physiologic leukorrhea: nonwatery discharge without amniotic-fluid markers

table.title: Stable PROM without delivery indication
rows: Oxytocin induction; brief expectant option after counseling
Delivery or expectant management; stop expectance by 37
Individualized counseling: termination versus expectance, maternal risks

primary-headaches.name: Primary headaches
primary-headaches.scope: Migraine, tension-type, cluster, medication-overuse headache, red flags
primary-headaches.core: Recurrent stereotyped headaches with normal neurologic examination favor a primary syndrome; a new dangerous pattern requires secondary-cause evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, sleep disruption, stress, hormonal fluctuation; alcohol triggers cluster bouts
Frequent rescue analgesic use promotes chronic daily headache

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Thunderclap, fever, papilledema, focal deficit, cancer, pregnancy/postpartum** → evaluate secondary cause
New headache after age 50, positional/Valsalva provocation, progressive change also concerning
Medication overuse: headache ≥15 days/month with sustained frequent acute-drug exposure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Migraine: trigeminovascular/CGRP signaling; aura: cortical spreading depolarization, visual → contralateral occipital lobe
Cluster: hypothalamic/autonomic activation; overuse sustains sensitization and rebound symptoms

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical stable primary pattern + normal exam → **no routine neuroimaging**
Thunderclap → head CT; negative with persistent SAH concern → LP or CTA
MRI for concerning nonemergent progressive patterns; fundoscopy and full neurologic examination
Overuse >3 months: triptans/opioids/combinations ≥10 days/month; acetaminophen/NSAIDs ≥15 days/month

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe migraine → **sumatriptan + naproxen**, metoclopramide for nausea; avoid triptans with ischemic vascular disease
Frequent migraine → propranolol, topiramate, CGRP drugs; pregnancy → **acetaminophen**; no ergots, topiramate, valproate
★ Cluster attack → **100% oxygen or subcutaneous sumatriptan**; prevention with verapamil, ECG monitoring
Tension headache → acetaminophen/NSAID; recurrent chronic disease → amitriptyline, behavioral treatment
Medication overuse → withdraw culprit, start prevention; taper opioids/barbiturates rather than abrupt withdrawal

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic migraine, functional disability, status migrainosus; analgesic toxicity
Estrogen-containing contraception increases stroke concern in migraine with aura
Triptan + **ergotamine within 24 hours** → additive vasoconstriction: prolonged vasospasm, MI, stroke

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Regular sleep/meals, exercise, headache diary**, limit rescue-drug days
Avoid opioids for routine primary headache; identify personal rather than universal dietary triggers
Migraine escalation after starting estrogen, normal exam → **stop estrogen** before imaging or added analgesics

rows.label: Mimics
items: GCA: age >50, jaw claudication/visual symptoms
Acute glaucoma: red painful eye, halos, high pressure; sinusitis: purulence and objective sinus findings

primary-headaches.evidence: Not checked online; established headache classification and generalist management.

primary-immunodeficiencies.name: Primary immunodeficiencies
primary-immunodeficiencies.scope: Selective IgA deficiency, common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), X-linked agammaglobulinemia, severe combined immunodeficiency, hyper-IgE syndrome, Wiskott-Aldrich, chronic granulomatous disease
primary-immunodeficiencies.core: Recurrent, unusually severe, persistent, or opportunistic infections; organism pattern and age of onset localize the immune defect.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Consanguinity, affected relatives, male relatives dying in infancy; absent family history does not exclude disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, persistent thrush, or infections across multiple organ systems
Deep abscesses suggest phagocyte dysfunction; recurrent encapsulated bacteria suggest impaired antibody function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Selective IgA deficiency: impaired mucosal defense; respiratory infections, giardiasis, atopy, or no symptoms
Antibody disorders impair opsonization; T-cell defects permit viral, fungal, and protozoal opportunists
DiGeorge: 3rd/4th **pharyngeal pouch** failure → absent thymus, hypocalcemia, conotruncal defects, T-cell infections
ADA deficiency: autosomal recessive SCID; toxic deoxyadenosine destroys T and B cells

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Start **CBC with differential, quantitative immunoglobulins**, HIV testing; assess vaccine antibody responses
Lymphocyte subsets distinguish B-cell and T-cell deficiencies; abnormal results → genetic confirmation
IgA deficiency: isolated IgA <7 mg/dL after age 4 years; normal IgG and IgM
★ Newborn **TREC screen** detects impaired T-cell production before symptomatic SCID

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Profound combined immune failure → isolation, irradiated CMV-negative blood products, urgent **transplant evaluation**
Acute infections: organism-directed antimicrobials; immunoglobulin replacement not useful for isolated IgA deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Bronchiectasis, chronic enteropathy, autoimmune disease; CVID additionally increases lymphoma risk
Anti-IgA antibodies can cause anaphylaxis to blood products

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Avoid **live vaccines** in major T-cell defects; immunize household contacts with safe vaccine choices
IgA-related transfusion reactions → washed cellular products or IgA-deficient plasma
CGD: TMP-SMX + itraconazole prophylaxis; genetic counseling for inherited defects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vertical HIV: bacterial infections + zoster, nodes, maternal opportunistic infection; low CD4, positive virologic testing
Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia: nephrotic protein loss, B-cell malignancy, or rituximab exposure

table.title: Defect fingerprints
rows: Adolescent/adult; low IgG, poor vaccine response
Boy after 6 months; absent tonsils/B cells
Infant; absent thymic shadow, profound lymphopenia
Cold abscesses, eczema, retained teeth, pneumatoceles

primary-immunodeficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical immunology teaching.

proteinuria.name: Proteinuria
proteinuria.scope: Transient proteinuria, orthostatic (postural) proteinuria, persistent proteinuria, split urine collection, spot protein-to-creatinine ratio, nephrology referral
proteinuria.core: Incidental urinary protein requires confirmation and quantification; persistence, sediment, renal function, and blood pressure distinguish benign variants from kidney disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Transient: fever, strenuous exercise, dehydration, seizures; orthostatic pattern common in adolescent males
Persistent: diabetes, hypertension, glomerulonephritis, systemic autoimmune disease, hereditary nephropathy

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic; foamy urine and periorbital/dependent edema suggest heavier losses
★ **Hematuria, hypertension, RBC casts, reduced eGFR**, or systemic rash/arthritis → pathologic renal process

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Glomerular permeability → albumin leakage; impaired tubular reabsorption → smaller proteins; overproduction → overflow

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Positive dipstick → **first-morning UA/microscopy and spot urine protein:creatinine ratio (UPCR)**
Pediatric normal UPCR: age >2 years **≤0.2 mg/mg**; age 6–24 months ≤0.5
Nephrotic range: children UPCR ≥2 mg/mg; adults total protein ≥3.5 g/day
★ Postural uncertainty → **split upright/supine collection**; separate daytime activity from overnight recumbency
Persistent abnormality → creatinine, albumin, BP; nephritic → complement/ANA; adults: spot albumin:creatinine

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Protein plus active sediment, impaired filtration, marked edema, or systemic disease → **nephrology referral**
Biopsy selected persistent unexplained cases, especially nephritic findings; do not biopsy benign postural pattern
